knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax+b\in K\) is the canonical conic feasibility constraint.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional affine cone-membership standard form.

source_refs.locator: 2.2 A primal-dual interior-point method p. 44

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An affine cone-membership problem has the form \[\operatorname{minimize}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\ c^{\mathsf T}x\qquad\operatorname{subject\ to}\qquad Ax+b\in K.\] Equalities and inequalities are represented by selecting suitable factors of \(K\), including the zero cone and nonnegative orthant. The feasible set is the inverse image \(\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax+b\in K\}\), hence is convex because \(K\) is convex and the constraint map is affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic model minimizes a linear objective over decisions whose affine image belongs to a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine Cone-Membership Forms

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2 A primal-dual interior-point method p. 44

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closedness of Affine Cone-Membership Feasible Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Topological property of the direct affine cone-membership form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax+b\in K\}\), convexity of \(K\) implies convexity of \(S\), and closedness of \(K\) implies closedness of \(S\). Thus a closed convex cone produces a closed convex feasible set under any affine preimage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine inverse image preserves convexity and closedness of the cone.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S=(x\mapsto Ax+b)^{-1}(K)\text{ is closed and convex}.
knowledge_statements.title: Closedness of Affine Cone-Membership Feasible Sets

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Product-Cone Aggregation of Affine Membership Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical aggregation of finitely many direct affine cone constraints into one membership constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For affine maps \(x\mapsto A_i x+b_i\) and cones \(K_i\), \[A_i x+b_i\in K_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,q)\] is equivalent to \[(A_1x+b_1,\ldots,A_qx+b_q)\in K_1\times\cdots\times K_q.\] Zero-cone factors encode equalities and orthant factors encode componentwise inequalities with the chosen sign orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite collection of affine conic constraints is one affine membership constraint in the product cone.
assumptions_latex: For each \(i\), \(A_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_i}\) is linear, \(b_i\in\mathbb R^{m_i}\), and \(K_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{m_i}\) is a cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigcap_{i=1}^q\{x:A_ix+b_i\in K_i\}=\{x:(A_ix+b_i)_{i=1}^q\in\prod_{i=1}^qK_i\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Product-Cone Aggregation of Affine Membership Constraints

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax+b\in K\) holds exactly when \(s=Ax+b\) for some \(s\in K\); equivalently, \(Ax+s=-b\) uses \(s\in -K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-plus-conic-slack form equivalent to affine membership, with the cone sign stated explicitly.

source_refs.locator: 2.2 A primal-dual interior-point method p. 44
source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The affine cone constraint \(Ax+b\in K\) admits the direct slack-variable representation \[s=Ax+b,\qquad s\in K.\] Equivalently, it can be written as \[Ax-s=-b,\qquad s\in K.\] If instead the equality is written as \(Ax+s=-b\), then the exact cone condition is \(s\in -K\). A canonicalizer must record the sign convention and the associated cone; each of these consistent conventions preserves the projected feasible set in \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine cone constraint can be replaced by a linear equality and a cone-constrained slack variable, provided the equality sign convention and the corresponding cone sign are recorded consistently.
knowledge_statements.title: Slack-Variable Conic Forms

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal data layout is the typed tuple \((A,b,c,K;x,s)\) with dimensions fixed by \((m,n)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Typed finite-dimensional storage layout for slack-form primal data.

source_refs.locator: 2.2 A primal-dual interior-point method p. 44

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the slack-form primal problem \[\operatorname{minimize}_{x,s}\ c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\operatorname{subject\ to}\quad Ax+s=b,\quad s\in K,\] a dimension-consistent primal layout stores \(A\) as an \(m\)-by-\(n\) operator, \(b\) and \(s\) in \(\mathbb{R}^m\), \(c\) and \(x\) in \(\mathbb{R}^n\), and cone metadata for \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\). Row coordinates of \(A\), \(b\), and \(s\) share the cone-block ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal storage aligns constraint rows, right-hand-side entries, slack coordinates, and cone metadata, while columns align with decisions and objective coefficients.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Data Layouts

children.title: Dual Data Layouts
children.top_down_role: Organization of dual variables, adjoint data, dual-cone blocks, and solver-facing records.

assumptions_latex: The primal problem is \(\operatorname{minimize} c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax+s=b\), with \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) free and \(s\in K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For the equality convention \(Ax+s=b\), a dual equality multiplier \(y\) satisfies \(A^{\mathsf T}y=c\) and \(y\in-K^*\); equivalently, \(\lambda=-y\in K^*\) satisfies \(A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=-c\).

notation.meaning: equality multiplier under the Ax+s=b convention

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual storage induced by the stated slack-form primal layout with a free primal decision vector.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal convention \[\operatorname{minimize}_{x,s}\ c^{\mathsf T}x\qquad\operatorname{subject\ to}\qquad Ax+s=b,\quad s\in K,\] with \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) free, the equality multiplier \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) satisfies \[A^{\mathsf T}y=c,\qquad y\in-K^*.\] Equivalently, the sign-adjusted variable \(\lambda=-y\in K^*\) satisfies \(A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=-c\). Dual storage uses the primal row ordering for \(y\), \(\lambda\), and the dual-cone metadata, while \(A^{\mathsf T}y\) and \(c\) use the primal column ordering. Because \(x\) is free, no additional reduced-cost vector is present in this form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the stated plus-slack primal convention, dual multipliers use primal row order and belong to the negative dual cone; after a sign change, the stored variable belongs to the dual cone. Adjoint products and objective coefficients use primal column order.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Data Layouts

children.title: Primal–Dual Layout Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural alignment between primal records, dual records, cone blocks, and recovery metadata.

assumptions_latex: Primal and dual forms use one fixed sign convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal block \(K_i\) corresponds coordinatewise to dual block \(K_i^*\), and \(A\) corresponds to \(A^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate correspondence for finite-dimensional primal-dual conic data.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K=K_1\times\cdots\times K_q\), then \[K^*=K_1^*\times\cdots\times K_q^*.\] Under a shared block ordering, the primal slack block \(s_i\in K_i\) and dual multiplier block \(y_i\in K_i^*\) occupy the same coordinate interval and contribute \(\langle s_i,y_i\rangle\) to complementarity. The primal constraint operator \(A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) and dual operator \(A^{\mathsf T}:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}^n\) exchange row and column layouts while preserving these coordinate pairings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each primal cone block pairs with its dual block on the same coordinates, and the primal matrix layout transposes for dual stationarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Layout Correspondence

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The homogeneous block product is \(K_0^q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{qd}\) with identical block dimensions and cone types.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cartesian products whose blocks share one cone type and dimension.

source_refs.locator: 3.3 The geometry of cone-lp's: main results p. 37

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A homogeneous cone-block product generated by \(K_0\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is \[K_0^q=\underbrace{K_0\times\cdots\times K_0}_{q\ \mathrm{factors}}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{qd}.\] A vector \(s=(s_1,\ldots,s_q)\) belongs to \(K_0^q\) exactly when \(s_i\in K_0\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,q\}\). Every block therefore has the same dimension, cone operations, and dual template; moreover, \((K_0^q)^*=(K_0^*)^q\) under the blockwise Euclidean inner product.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A homogeneous product cone consists of equally sized blocks, all belonging to the same cone template.
knowledge_statements.title: Homogeneous Cone-Block Products

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Permutation symmetry of a Cartesian power of one cone template.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_0\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), let \(q\ge1\), and let \(P_\pi\) permute the \(q\) complete blocks of \((\mathbb R^d)^q\). Then \(P_\pi(K_0^q)=K_0^q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every whole-block permutation preserves a homogeneous product cone.
review_flags: deferred_misplaced: the claim is mathematically correct but its primary canonical home is the sibling Permutation Stability Boundaries leaf
cross_index_preferred: homogeneous products provide the important special case of the general permutation-invariance condition
knowledge_statements.title: Block-Permutation Invariance

intermediate_metadata.reason: The seed exhausts the homogeneous product's local definition, membership test, common template, and dual. The proposed block-permutation claim is deferred as primarily owned by Permutation Stability Boundaries; heterogeneous products, batching, addressing, and execution are likewise excluded adjacent scopes.

assumptions_latex: For \(i=1,\ldots,q\), \(K_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d_i}\) is a closed convex cone.
At least two factors may differ in type or dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The heterogeneous product is \(K_1\times\cdots\times K_q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{\sum_i d_i}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cartesian products allowing distinct cone types and dimensions.

source_refs.locator: 3.3 The geometry of cone-lp's: main results p. 37

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The heterogeneous cone-block product of the ordered family \((K_i)_{i=1}^q\) is \[K=\prod_{i=1}^q K_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{D},\qquad D=\sum_{i=1}^q d_i.\] With the corresponding coordinate partition, \(s\in K\) exactly when each block \(s_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d_i}\) satisfies \(s_i\in K_i\). The block order and dimensions are part of the representation. Under blockwise Euclidean pairings, the dual cone is \(K^*=\prod_{i=1}^q K_i^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A heterogeneous product cone concatenates ordered blocks that may have different cone types and dimensions; membership and dualization are blockwise.
knowledge_statements.title: Heterogeneous Cone-Block Products

children.title: Repeated Cone-Block Templates
children.top_down_role: Reusable organization of multiple cone blocks sharing a common type and dimension pattern.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The template \((K_0,d,q)\) expands to \(q\) ordered copies of \(K_0\) on consecutive intervals.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Cartesian-power representation and consecutive block expansion are standard modeling conventions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact metadata representation for repeated identical cone factors.

source_refs.locator: 3.3 The geometry of cone-lp's: main results p. 37

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A repeated cone-block template is the tuple \((K_0,d,q)\), where \(K_0\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) and \(q\geq1\). Its expansion is \(K_0^q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{qd}\), with block intervals \[I_i=\{(i-1)d+1,\ldots,id\},\qquad i=1,\ldots,q.\] For a stored vector \(s\in\mathbb{R}^{qd}\), the slice \(s_{I_i}\) is interpreted using the same cone-membership, projection, scaling, and dual-cone rules for every block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A repeated template stores one cone type, one block dimension, and a multiplicity, then expands them into consecutive identical blocks.
knowledge_statements.title: Repeated Cone-Block Templates

children.title: Batched Cone-Block Layouts
children.top_down_role: Grouped storage and solver-facing representation of cone-block batches.

assumptions_latex: Batch \(r\) contains \(q_r\) blocks of a cone \(K_r\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d_r}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The batched layout represents \(\prod_{r=1}^p K_r^{q_r}\) by concatenating all blocks of each batch.

notation.meaning: cone template and multiplicity of batch r
dimension of each block in batch r

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: batching repeated Cartesian factors is a conventional equivalent storage representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contiguous grouping of repeated cone templates into ordered batches.

source_refs.locator: 3.3 The geometry of cone-lp's: main results p. 37

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A batched cone-block layout for templates \((K_r,d_r,q_r)\), indexed by \(r=1,\ldots,p\), represents \[K=\prod_{r=1}^p K_r^{q_r}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{D},\qquad D=\sum_{r=1}^p q_r d_r.\] Coordinates are concatenated first by batch index and then by copy index within each batch. Thus every batch occupies one contiguous interval of length \(q_r d_r\), and that interval decomposes into \(q_r\) consecutive blocks of length \(d_r\). Membership in \(K\) is equivalent to membership of every decoded block in its batch template.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A batched layout groups consecutive copies of each cone template and concatenates the resulting batches in a fixed order.
knowledge_statements.title: Batched Cone-Block Layouts

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3 The geometry of cone-lp's: main results p. 37

children.title: Batch Boundary Metadata
children.top_down_role: Offsets, block boundaries, multiplicities, and batch membership records.

assumptions_latex: Batch \(r\) has block dimension \(d_r\) and multiplicity \(q_r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Offsets \(o_0=0\) and \(o_r=\sum_{t=1}^r q_t d_t\) uniquely delimit every batch.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: prefix offsets are the standard exact metadata for contiguous variable-length partitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prefix-offset metadata for recovering batch and block boundaries.

source_refs.locator: 3.3 The geometry of cone-lp's: main results p. 37

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For ordered batches \(r=1,\ldots,p\), define \[o_0=0,\qquad o_r=o_{r-1}+q_r d_r.\] Batch \(r\) occupies the half-open coordinate interval \([o_{r-1},o_r)\). Its copy \(j\in\{0,\ldots,q_r-1\}\) occupies \[\bigl[o_{r-1}+jd_r,\ o_{r-1}+(j+1)d_r\bigr).\] The metadata \((o_r,d_r,q_r)_{r=1}^p\), together with each cone template, therefore determines a disjoint, exhaustive partition of the stored vector coordinates and permits deterministic recovery of every block boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cumulative offsets, block dimensions, and multiplicities determine all batch and within-batch coordinate boundaries without ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.title: Batch Boundary Metadata

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3 The geometry of cone-lp's: main results p. 37

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of batch, copy, and within-copy coordinates from valid batch-boundary metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0=o_0<o_1<\cdots<o_p=D\) with \(o_r-o_{r-1}=q_rd_r\), where \(q_r,d_r\ge1\). Given \(g\in\{0,\ldots,D-1\}\), find the unique \(r\) satisfying \(o_{r-1}\le g<o_r\). Set \(u=g-o_{r-1}\) and compute \[j=\left\lfloor\frac{u}{d_r}\right\rfloor,\qquad \ell=u-jd_r.\] Then \((r,j,\ell)\) is the unique batch, copy, and local-coordinate address of \(g\). Binary search on the offsets uses \(O(\log p)\) comparisons, followed by constant-time arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary search in cumulative batch offsets followed by quotient-remainder decoding uniquely recovers a coordinate's batch, copy, and local position.
assumptions_latex: The offset array supports random access.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g\longleftrightarrow(r,j,\ell)\text{ is uniquely decoded using }O(\log p)\text{ comparisons}.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: predecessor search and Euclidean division invert contiguous fixed-width batching
knowledge_statements.title: Batch and Copy Decoding

children.title: Cone-Block Ordering
children.top_down_role: Sequencing conventions for homogeneous and heterogeneous cone blocks.

assumptions_latex: A total order \(\prec\) is fixed on their labels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ordering determines a unique concatenation of block coordinates and cone factors.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: an ordered Cartesian product requires a permutation and corresponding coordinate concatenation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total ordering used to serialize labeled cone factors.

source_refs.locator: 3.3 The geometry of cone-lp's: main results p. 37

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cone-block ordering is a permutation \(\pi\) of \(\{1,\ldots,q\}\) specifying the serialized product \[K_{\pi(1)}\times\cdots\times K_{\pi(q)}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{\sum_{i=1}^q d_i}.\] The coordinate vector is concatenated in the same order: \(s=(s_{\pi(1)},\ldots,s_{\pi(q)})\), where \(s_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d_i}\). The ordering is representation data rather than a change to the abstract product; every aligned object, including constraint rows, slacks, dual multipliers, and cone metadata, must use the identical permutation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone-block ordering is a permutation that fixes how blocks and every row-aligned primal-dual object are serialized.
knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Block Ordering

children.title: Cone-Block Coordinate Indexing
children.top_down_role: Coordinate ranges, block offsets, and local-to-global index organization.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each pair \((k,j)\) maps bijectively to global coordinate \(g=o_k+j\).

notation.meaning: prefix offset of ordered block k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: prefix-sum indexing is the canonical bijection for concatenated variable-length blocks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bijection between block-local and serialized global coordinates.

source_refs.locator: 3.3 The geometry of cone-lp's: main results p. 37

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define prefix offsets \[o_1=0,\qquad o_k=\sum_{t=1}^{k-1}d_{\pi(t)}\quad\text{for }k=2,\ldots,q.\] For ordered block position \(k\) and local zero-based coordinate \(j\in\{0,\ldots,d_{\pi(k)}-1\}\), the global coordinate is \[g=o_k+j.\] These intervals are disjoint and cover \(\{0,\ldots,\sum_i d_i-1\}\), so the mapping is bijective. Conversely, the unique \(k\) satisfying \(o_k\leq g<o_k+d_{\pi(k)}\) identifies the block, and \(j=g-o_k\) recovers its local coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prefix offsets map each block position and local coordinate bijectively to a global serialized coordinate, and interval lookup provides the inverse.
knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Block Coordinate Indexing

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3 The geometry of cone-lp's: main results p. 37

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithmic recovery of a block-local address from a global serialized coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(o_1=0<o_2<\cdots<o_{q+1}=D\), where \(o_{k+1}=o_k+d_{\pi(k)}\) and every \(d_{\pi(k)}\ge1\). For \(g\in\{0,\ldots,D-1\}\), binary search for the unique \(k\) satisfying \(o_k\le g<o_{k+1}\), then return \((k,g-o_k)\). The lookup uses \(O(\log q)\) comparisons and \(O(1)\) auxiliary space; forward evaluation \(g=o_k+j\) uses \(O(1)\) time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary search in stored prefix offsets recovers the unique block and local coordinate in logarithmic time; forward indexing is constant time.
assumptions_latex: The prefix-offset array \((o_k)_{k=1}^{q+1}\) supports random access.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((k,j)\) is recovered uniquely using \(O(\log q)\) comparisons.

notation.meaning: start offset of ordered block k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: predecessor search in a strictly increasing prefix-offset array finds the unique containing interval
knowledge_statements.title: Inverse Coordinate Lookup

children.title: Ordering-to-Index Mappings
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between symbolic block order and solver-data coordinates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence from symbolic block labels and their order to solver-data block positions and contiguous coordinate slices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\) be a finite set of block labels and let \(\pi:\{1,\ldots,q\}\to L\) be the bijection specifying their serialized order. Define the position map \(p=\pi^{-1}\) and offsets \(s_1=0\), \(s_{k+1}=s_k+d_{\pi(k)}\). The solver slice assigned to label \(i\in L\) is \[S(i)=\{s_{p(i)},\ldots,s_{p(i)+1}-1\}.\] Thus \(i\mapsto(p(i),S(i))\) bijectively associates every symbolic block with one ordered solver block and one contiguous coordinate slice. Every block-indexed solver-data object must use this same association.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inverse ordering map assigns each symbolic block label a unique solver position and contiguous coordinate slice shared by all aligned data objects.
assumptions_latex: Each label \(i\in L\) has a declared positive coordinate dimension \(d_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: i\longmapsto\bigl(p(i),S(i)\bigr)\text{ is a bijective label-to-solver-block correspondence}.

notation.meaning: solver coordinate slice assigned to label i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: inverting the symbolic ordering and attaching its prefix interval gives the canonical label-to-solver-slice correspondence
distinguished_from_coordinate_indexing: this record maps semantic labels to solver block positions and slices rather than local scalar coordinates to global indices
knowledge_statements.title: Block Labels to Solver Slices
Ordering-to-Index Mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maps an ordered product-cone block structure to contiguous scalar-coordinate addresses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=K_1\times\cdots\times K_q\), where \(q\in\mathbb N\), block \(K_i\) has coordinate dimension \(d_i\in\mathbb N\), and \(\pi\) is a permutation of \(\{1,\ldots,q\}\). Define \(s_1=0\) and \(s_{k+1}=s_k+d_{\pi(k)}\) for \(k\in\{1,\ldots,q\}\), and let \(D_\pi=\{(k,j):1\le k\le q,\ 1\le j\le d_{\pi(k)}\}\). In the ordering \((K_{\pi(1)},\ldots,K_{\pi(q)})\), define \[I_\pi:D_\pi\to\left\{1,\ldots,\sum_{i=1}^q d_i\right\},\qquad I_\pi(k,j)=s_k+j.\] The intervals \(\{s_k+1,\ldots,s_{k+1}\}\) are pairwise disjoint and partition \(\{1,\ldots,\sum_{i=1}^q d_i\}\); hence \(I_\pi\) is a bijection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cumulative block dimensions assign every local cone coordinate a unique contiguous global index, and the resulting block intervals partition the full coordinate vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I_\pi:D_\pi\to\{1,\ldots,\sum_{i=1}^q d_i\}\) is a bijection.

starting offset of the kth ordered block
set of ordered-block and local-coordinate pairs

children.title: Permutation Stability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Representation effects arising from reordered blocks, coordinates, or metadata.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete loss of feasibility caused by reordering heterogeneous block descriptors without the corresponding coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\mathbb R_+\times Q_2\), where \(Q_2=\{(t,x)\in\mathbb R^2:t\ge |x|\}\), and serialize blocks in the order \((\mathbb R_+,Q_2)\). The vector \(z=(\tfrac12,1,0)\) is feasible. If the metadata is changed to \((Q_2,\mathbb R_+)\) while the coordinates remain unchanged, the same array is decoded as \(((\tfrac12,1),0)\), which is infeasible because \(\tfrac12<|1|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible heterogeneous cone vector can become infeasible when block metadata is reordered without reordering its coordinates.
assumptions_latex: Coordinates are not permuted when the block descriptors are reordered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\tfrac12,1,0)\in\mathbb R_+\times Q_2\quad\text{but}\quad(\tfrac12,1,0)\notin Q_2\times\mathbb R_+.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct membership evaluation demonstrates metadata-coordinate desynchronization
knowledge_statements.title: Block-Metadata Desynchronization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes equivalent coordinated reindexing from reuse of an unchanged cone descriptor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and let \(P\) be a permutation matrix. Coordinated reindexing always satisfies \[z\in K\iff Pz\in PK.\] If the stored cone descriptor is left unchanged as \(K\), then the reordered interface has the same membership domain exactly when \(PK=K\). Accordingly, a permutation may be a valid change of representation without being an automorphism of the unchanged cone descriptor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transforming both coordinates and the cone gives an equivalent representation for every permutation; keeping the cone descriptor unchanged is safe exactly for cone-preserving permutations.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a cone represented in fixed coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z\in K\iff Pz\in PK,\qquad \{z:Pz\in K\}=K\iff PK=K.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: bijective coordinate changes preserve membership when the represented set is transformed with the coordinates
clarifies_boundary: equivalence under coordinated reindexing is distinct from invariance of an unchanged cone descriptor
knowledge_statements.title: Coordinated Reindexing versus Cone Invariance
Permutation Stability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes when coordinate permutations preserve a product-cone domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a product cone and let \(P\) be a permutation matrix. Reindexing variables, constraint rows, and cone coordinates consistently replaces membership \(z\in K\) by \(Pz\in PK\). It leaves the encoded cone unchanged exactly when \(PK=K\). Block permutations between identical cone factors, together with automorphic within-block permutations, satisfy this condition. Arbitrary coordinate permutations need not: for the second-order cone \(Q_3=\{(t,x_1,x_2):\sqrt{x_1^2+x_2^2}\le t\}\), swapping \(t\) and \(x_1\) does not preserve \(Q_3\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A permutation is representation-stable exactly when it maps the cone onto itself; mixing structurally distinct coordinates can change feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original and permuted membership interfaces have the same domain if and only if \(PK=K\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: invariance of a set under reindexing is exactly the condition PK=K

children.title: Free-Cone Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Modeling and solver-facing treatment of unrestricted variable domains.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonicalization rule for a constraint-side block equal to its whole ambient space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a conic model contains a block whose only requirement is \(u(x)\in\mathbb R^m\) for an affine expression \(u\), the block may be deleted without changing the primal feasible set or objective value. In the corresponding dual representation its multiplier is fixed to \(0\in\{0\}^m\). Reintroducing the block with zero multiplier recovers the uncondensed primal-dual layout.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A free cone-constraint block is primal-redundant and can be removed, with its dual multiplier fixed to zero.
assumptions_latex: The block has no side conditions beyond membership in \(\mathbb R^m\).
The Euclidean dual convention is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The free block may be removed without changing primal feasibility or value, and its dual multiplier satisfies \(y_{\mathrm{free}}=0\).

notation.meaning: dual multiplier associated with the removed free block

knowledge_statements.title: Elimination of Free Cone-Constraint Blocks
Free-Cone Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the unrestricted vector block used by a conic canonicalization interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m\in\mathbb N\), the free cone is the vector space \(K_{\mathrm{free}}^m=\mathbb R^m\), regarded as a convex cone. An affine expression \(u(x)=Ax+b\in\mathbb R^m\) connected to this interface satisfies \(u(x)\in K_{\mathrm{free}}^m\) for every value of \(u(x)\); hence the block imposes no primal feasibility restriction. Under the Euclidean pairing, its dual cone is \((K_{\mathrm{free}}^m)^*=\{0\}^m\), so the associated dual block must vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A free-cone block accepts every real vector, imposes no primal restriction, and has the zero cone as its dual.
assumptions_latex: The dual uses the Euclidean inner product
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u(x)\in\mathbb R^m\) is unrestricted and \((\mathbb R^m)^*=\{0\}^m\).

notation.meaning: affine expression supplied to the cone interface

children.title: Zero-Cone Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Modeling and solver-facing treatment of affine equality domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Cone Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines equality constraints as membership in a zero-cone block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m\in\mathbb N\), define the zero cone by \(K_0^m=\{0\}^m\subseteq\mathbb R^m\). Connecting an affine expression \(u(x)=Ax+b\in\mathbb R^m\) to the zero-cone interface means \[u(x)\in K_0^m\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad Ax+b=0.\] Thus the interface encodes exactly \(m\) scalar affine equalities. Under the Euclidean pairing, \((K_0^m)^*=\mathbb R^m\), so its dual variables are unrestricted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Membership in the zero cone is exactly an affine equality; its associated dual vector is unrestricted.
assumptions_latex: The dual uses the Euclidean inner product
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax+b\in K_0^m\) if and only if \(Ax+b=0\), and \((K_0^m)^*=\mathbb R^m\).

notation.meaning: affine residual supplied to the interface

children.title: Orthant-Cone Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Modeling and solver-facing treatment of componentwise sign domains.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise feasibility and complementarity certificate for a nonnegative-orthant block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s,y\in\mathbb R^m\) be the primal slack and dual variable for a nonnegative-orthant block under the Euclidean self-dual convention. Exact cone feasibility and complementarity are equivalent to \[s_i\ge0,\qquad y_i\ge0,\qquad s_i y_i=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\] Equivalently, \(s,y\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and \(\langle s,y\rangle=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an orthant block, primal-dual feasibility and complementarity reduce to nonnegative coordinates with zero coordinatewise products.
assumptions_latex: The block uses the nonnegative orthant and Euclidean self-duality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s,y\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and \(\langle s,y\rangle=0\iff s_i y_i=0\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.title: Orthant Primal-Dual Complementarity Test

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Orthant Interface Interior and Active Face
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-facing interpretation of strict, boundary, and active coordinates in an orthant block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m\ge1\), \[\operatorname{int}\mathbb R_+^m=\{u:u_i>0\ \forall i\},\qquad \partial\mathbb R_+^m=\{u\ge0:u_i=0\ \text{for some }i\}.\] For \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \[F_I=\{u\ge0:u_i=0\ \forall i\in I\}\] is a face, and every face of \(\mathbb R_+^m\) has this form. Thus the zero slack coordinates identify the active face of an orthant interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict positivity gives the orthant interior, while zero slack coordinates identify its boundary face and active inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The faces of \(\mathbb R_+^m\) are exactly the coordinate-zero sets \(F_I\).

notation.meaning: orthant face indexed by forced-zero coordinates

knowledge_statements.title: Orthant Interface Interior and Active Face
Orthant-Cone Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents componentwise affine inequalities through nonnegative or nonpositive orthant membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m\in\mathbb N\), let \(K_+^m=\mathbb R_+^m=\{u\in\mathbb R^m:u_i\ge0\text{ for all }i\}\). An affine inequality system \(Ax+b\ge0\), interpreted componentwise, is represented exactly by \(Ax+b\in K_+^m\). Likewise, \(Ax+b\le0\) is represented by \(-(Ax+b)\in K_+^m\), or equivalently by membership in \(-K_+^m\). Under the Euclidean pairing, \((K_+^m)^*=K_+^m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Componentwise affine inequalities are exactly orthant-membership constraints, with a sign reversal converting nonpositive to nonnegative form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax+b\ge0\Longleftrightarrow Ax+b\in\mathbb R_+^m\), and \((\mathbb R_+^m)^*=\mathbb R_+^m\).

children.title: Polyhedral-Cone Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Modeling interfaces for general finitely represented polyhedral cone domains.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-cone descriptions induced directly by exact inequality and generator interfaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K=\{u\in\mathbb R^m:Hu\ge0\}\), then \(K^*=\{H^Ty:y\in\mathbb R_+^r\}\). If \(K=\{V\lambda:\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^s\}\), then \(K^*=\{z\in\mathbb R^m:V^Tz\ge0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact inequality interface dualizes to nonnegative combinations of its row normals, while an exact generator interface dualizes to one nonnegative inner-product inequality per generator.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb R^{r\times m}\) and \(V\in\mathbb R^{m\times s}\) give exact representations of \(K\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K^*=H^T\mathbb R_+^r\quad\text{or}\quad K^*=\{z:V^Tz\ge0\},

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Interfaces for Polyhedral Cones
Polyhedral-Cone Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies inequality and generator interfaces for closed convex polyhedral cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is polyhedral when there is a matrix \(H\in\mathbb R^{r\times m}\) such that \(K=\{u:Hu\ge0\}\). Equivalently, there is a matrix \(V\in\mathbb R^{m\times s}\) such that \(K=\{V\lambda:\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^s\}\). Hence an affine expression \(u(x)=Ax+b\) may be interfaced either directly by \(H(Ax+b)\in\mathbb R_+^r\), or through auxiliary \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^s\) satisfying \(Ax+b=V\lambda\). Both interfaces express \(u(x)\in K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral-cone constraint can use either homogeneous linear inequalities or nonnegative generator coefficients, with auxiliary variables in the latter form.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a closed convex polyhedral cone
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u(x)\in K\) is equivalent to its stated inequality interface and, for a generator matrix, to the stated lifted interface.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Cone Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical affine interface for Lorentz-cone and rotated-Lorentz-cone constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\ge2\), define the second-order cone \(Q_n=\{(t,u)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{n-1}:\lVert u\rVert_2\le t\}\). Thus affine expressions \(t(x)\) and \(u(x)\) satisfy a second-order cone constraint exactly when \((t(x),u(x))\in Q_n\). The rotated interface uses \(Q_n^r=\{(a,b,u):a\ge0,\ b\ge0,\ 2ab\ge\lVert u\rVert_2^2\}\), with \(u\in\mathbb R^{n-2}\). It is linearly isomorphic to \(Q_n\) via \((a,b,u)\mapsto(a+b,a-b,\sqrt2u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Norm inequalities use Lorentz-cone membership; rotated cones encode nonnegative product bounds and are linearly equivalent to ordinary second-order cones.
assumptions_latex: All interface expressions are affine and dimensionally compatible
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert u(x)\rVert_2\le t(x)\Longleftrightarrow(t(x),u(x))\in Q_n\), with the stated rotated-cone equivalent.

knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Cone Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical matrix and packed-vector interfaces for positive-semidefinite affine constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbb S^n\) be the real symmetric matrices and \(\mathbb S_+^n=\{X\in\mathbb S^n:v^TXv\ge0\text{ for every }v\in\mathbb R^n\}\). For symmetric matrices \(F_0,\ldots,F_p\), the affine matrix inequality \(F_0+\sum_{i=1}^p x_iF_i\succeq0\) is exactly membership in \(\mathbb S_+^n\). A vectorized interface may use the isometry \(\operatorname{svec}:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^{n(n+1)/2}\), scaling off-diagonal entries by \(\sqrt2\); then the accepted vector cone is \(\operatorname{svec}(\mathbb S_+^n)\), preserving Frobenius inner products.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear matrix inequality is positive-semidefinite cone membership; packed storage should use a declared symmetric vectorization convention.
assumptions_latex: The packed interface uses the stated \(\operatorname{svec}\) convention
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_0+\sum_i x_iF_i\succeq0\) is equivalent to membership in \(\mathbb S_+^n\) or its stated packed-vector image.

notation.meaning: cone of real positive-semidefinite symmetric matrices

children.title: Exponential-Cone Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Modeling, domain, and solver-data interfaces for exponential-cone representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean dual cone for the declared primal coordinate order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the declared primal exponential cone, \[K_{\exp}^*=\left\{(u,v,w):u<0,\ -u\exp\!\left(\frac vu-1\right)\le w\right\}\cup\left\{(0,v,w):v\ge0,\ w\ge0\right\}.\] Thus the standard primal exponential cone is not self-dual; equivalent solver conventions may rescale or permute these coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exponential cone has a distinct explicitly scaled Euclidean dual and is not self-dual in standard coordinates.
assumptions_latex: Duality uses the Euclidean inner product.
The primal coordinates use the immutable \((x,y,z)\) convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_{\exp}^*\ne K_{\exp}\), with \(K_{\exp}^*\) equal to the displayed closed cone.
review_flags: Implementations may expose an equivalent rescaled or permuted dual convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Exponential-Cone Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical affine slices of the closed primal exponential-cone interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under \(K_{\exp}=\operatorname{cl}\{(a,b,c):b>0,\ b e^{a/b}\le c\}\), \[t\ge e^s\iff(s,1,t)\in K_{\exp}.\] For the closed extended-value relative-entropy convention, \[t\ge x\log(x/y)\iff(-t,x,y)\in K_{\exp}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exponential epigraphs and closed perspective relative-entropy epigraphs are direct slices of the exponential cone.
assumptions_latex: Relative entropy uses its closed extended-value convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exponential epigraph and closed perspective-relative-entropy epigraph are affine slices of \(K_{\exp}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exponential and Relative-Entropy Slices
Exponential-Cone Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the closed primal exponential cone and its affine membership interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The closed exponential cone is \[K_{\exp}=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:y>0,\ y\exp(x/y)\le z\}\cup\{(x,0,z):x\le0,\ z\ge0\}.\] For affine scalar expressions \(x(w),y(w),z(w)\), an exponential-cone interface accepts their ordered triple precisely when \((x(w),y(w),z(w))\in K_{\exp}\). The second set is the closure boundary at \(y=0\); omitting it produces the nonclosed perspective epigraph rather than the closed cone normally required by conic solvers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exponential-cone interface uses the closed perspective epigraph of the exponential, including its explicit zero-perspective boundary.
assumptions_latex: The interface uses the closed primal cone
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The affine triple is feasible exactly under the displayed interior or closure-boundary conditions.

children.title: Power-Cone Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Modeling, parameter, and solver-data interfaces for power-cone representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean dual of the declared three-dimensional power cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\alpha<1\), \[\left(K_{\mathrm{pow}}^\alpha\right)^*=\left\{(u,v,w):u\ge0,\ v\ge0,\ \left(\frac{u}{\alpha}\right)^\alpha\left(\frac{v}{1-\alpha}\right)^{1-\alpha}\ge|w|\right\}.\] Equivalently, \((u,v,w)\in(K_{\mathrm{pow}}^\alpha)^*\) exactly when \((u/\alpha,v/(1-\alpha),w)\in K_{\mathrm{pow}}^\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Euclidean dual power cone is a diagonally scaled copy of the primal power cone.
assumptions_latex: Duality uses the Euclidean inner product and the declared coordinate order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((K_{\mathrm{pow}}^\alpha)^*=\operatorname{diag}(\alpha,1-\alpha,1)K_{\mathrm{pow}}^\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Power-Cone Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Required exponent-metadata transformation when interchanging the two nonnegative coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(0<\alpha<1\), \[(x,y,z)\in K_{\mathrm{pow}}^\alpha\iff(y,x,z)\in K_{\mathrm{pow}}^{1-\alpha}.\] Hence swapping the first two coordinates without replacing \(\alpha\) by \(1-\alpha\) generally changes the represented cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Swapping the first two power-cone coordinates requires complementing the exponent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_{\mathrm{pow}}^{1-\alpha}=\{(y,x,z):(x,y,z)\in K_{\mathrm{pow}}^\alpha\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Power-Cone Coordinate-Swap Equivalence
Power-Cone Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the three-dimensional primal power cone for a fixed exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). The three-dimensional power cone is \[K_{\mathrm{pow}}^\alpha=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:x\ge0,\ y\ge0,\ x^\alpha y^{1-\alpha}\ge |z|\}.\] For affine scalar expressions \(x(w),y(w),z(w)\), the power-cone interface imposes membership of their ordered triple in \(K_{\mathrm{pow}}^\alpha\). The exponent \(\alpha\) is part of the cone-block metadata and must remain associated with that block under canonicalization or permutation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A power-cone block enforces nonnegative first coordinates and bounds the absolute third coordinate by their weighted geometric mean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x(w),y(w),z(w))\in K_{\mathrm{pow}}^\alpha\) exactly when the displayed inequalities hold.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric-Mean-Cone Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the symmetric hypograph convention for an n-variable geometric-mean cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\ge1\), define the symmetric geometric-mean cone by \[K_{\mathrm{gm}}^n=\left\{(x,t)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R:x_i\ge0\ \text{for all }i,\ |t|\le\left(\prod_{i=1}^n x_i\right)^{1/n}\right\}.\] An interface receiving affine expressions \(x(w)\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(t(w)\in\mathbb R\) imposes \((x(w),t(w))\in K_{\mathrm{gm}}^n\). If only the ordinary hypograph \(t\le(\prod_i x_i)^{1/n}\) is intended, the absolute value must be removed and that asymmetric convention declared separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The symmetric geometric-mean cone bounds an absolute scalar by the geometric mean of nonnegative coordinates; asymmetric hypograph conventions must be distinguished.
assumptions_latex: The symmetric absolute-value convention is used
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Membership is equivalent to nonnegativity of every \(x_i\) and the displayed geometric-mean bound on \(|t|\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometric-Mean Convention Mismatch at a Zero Coordinate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary witness distinguishing symmetric and asymmetric geometric-mean interfaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R_+^n\) have \(x_j=0\) for some \(j\). Then \((\prod_i x_i)^{1/n}=0\). The symmetric convention \(|t|\le(\prod_i x_i)^{1/n}\) forces \(t=0\), whereas the asymmetric convention \(t\le(\prod_i x_i)^{1/n}\) admits every \(t\le0\). Thus \((x,-1)\) is admitted by the asymmetric convention and rejected by the symmetric convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a zero input coordinate, symmetric and asymmetric geometric-mean interfaces have different scalar boundaries.
assumptions_latex: \(n\ge1\), \(x\ge0\), and at least one coordinate of \(x\) is zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,-1)\in K_{\mathrm{gm,asym}}\) but \((x,-1)\notin K_{\mathrm{gm,sym}}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter boundary for standard three-dimensional power-cone metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The standard three-dimensional power-cone interface requires \(0<\alpha<1\). At \(\alpha=0\) or \(\alpha=1\), the weighted product loses dependence on one factor and the usual dual scaling by \(\alpha\) and \(1-\alpha\) becomes singular. Endpoint cases must be represented by their explicit degenerate cones rather than passed to an interior-parameter power-cone oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard power-cone exponents lie strictly between zero and one; endpoint limits require separate degenerate cone blocks.
assumptions_latex: The interface uses the standard three-dimensional power-cone parameterization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha\notin(0,1)\) is inadmissible metadata for the standard power-cone block.

Nonlinear-Cone Domain Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies closure faces where interior nonlinear formulas cease to be directly evaluable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the closed exponential cone, the perspective formula \(y\exp(x/y)\le z\) applies only when \(y>0\); its finite closure at \(y=0\) is exactly \(x\le0\) and \(z\ge0\). For \(K_{\mathrm{pow}}^\alpha\) with \(0<\alpha<1\), if \(x=0\) or \(y=0\), membership forces \(z=0\). Thus canonicalizers must test these closed boundary predicates rather than evaluate division, logarithms, or negative powers there. Declaring only the strict-domain formulas excludes valid cone points and changes the represented feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closed nonlinear cones contain valid boundary points where interior perspective or power formulas are undefined; explicit boundary predicates preserve the intended feasible set.
assumptions_latex: The closed primal exponential cone convention is used
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Boundary membership is governed by the stated limiting predicates, not by direct evaluation of interior-only formulas.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convexity and Closedness of Direct Cone Preimages

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_A=\{(x,z)\in E\times F:z\in K,\ x=Az\}\). knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(K)=\operatorname{proj}_E\{(x,z)\in E\times F:z\in K,\ x=Az\}\), and every coordinate projection is a linear image.

knowledge_statements.title: Closedness under Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of closedness for a linear image of a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\mathbb S_+^2\) and define \(A:\mathbb S^2\to\mathbb R^2\) by \(A(X)=(X_{11},X_{12})\). Although \(K\) is a closed convex cone, \[A(K)=\{(a,b)\in\mathbb R^2:a>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\}\] is not closed. In particular, \((1/n,1)\in A(K)\) for every integer \(n\ge1\), whereas its limit \((0,1)\) does not belong to \(A(K)\). Thus a linear image, and hence a coordinate projection, of a closed convex cone need not be closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed semidefinite cone can have a nonclosed coordinate projection, so projection does not generally preserve closedness.
assumptions_latex: \(K=\mathbb S_+^2\) is the cone of real positive-semidefinite symmetric matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(K)=\{(a,b)\in\mathbb R^2:a>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\}\) is not closed.

Partial-Minimization Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-valued convex functions represented by minimizing a linear objective over a conic lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A partial-minimization conic representation of a function \(f:E\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty,-\infty\}\) is \[f(x)=d(x)+\inf_{y\in F}\{c(y):Ax+By+b\in K\},\] where the infimum of an empty feasible set is \(+\infty\). With \(\operatorname{dom}f:=\{x\in E:f(x)<+\infty\}\), \[\operatorname{dom}f=\{x\in E:\exists y\in F,\ Ax+By+b\in K\}.\] If the infimum is attained whenever \(f(x)\in\mathbb R\), then \[\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,t)\in E\times\mathbb R:\exists y\in F,\ Ax+By+b\in K,\ d(x)+c(y)\le t\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function has a partial-minimization conic representation when its value is the infimum of a linear expression over auxiliary variables satisfying affine conic constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(A:E\to G\) and \(B:F\to G\) are linear, with \(b\in G\), \(c\in F^*\), and \(d\in E^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)=d(x)+\inf\{c(y):y\in F,\ Ax+By+b\in K\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonattainment Boundary for the Epigraph Lift
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-cone example showing why attainment is required for the seed's exact existential epigraph formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_r^3=\{(u,v,w):u\ge0,\ v\ge0,\ 2uv\ge w^2\}\) and define \[f=\inf_{u,v}\{u:(u,v,1)\in K_r^3\}.\] Then \(f=0\), but no feasible pair attains \(u=0\). Consequently \[\{t:\exists u,v,\ (u,v,1)\in K_r^3,\ u\le t\}=(0,+\infty),\] whereas \(\operatorname{epi}f=[0,+\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even over a closed convex cone, a finite partial-minimization infimum can be unattained, causing the direct existential epigraph lift to omit its lower boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(K_r^3\) is the three-dimensional rotated second-order cone.
The auxiliary variables \(u,v\) are constrained only by \((u,v,1)\in K_r^3\).

knowledge_statements.title: Standard Lorentz-Cone Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard Euclidean second-order cone under the scalar-first convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer \(m\ge1\), the standard Lorentz cone is \[\mathcal Q^m=\{(t,x)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{m-1}:\|x\|_2\le t\}.\] Given an integer \(p\ge0\), a variable \(z\in\mathbb R^p\), data \(a\in\mathbb R^p\), \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{(m-1)\times p}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^{m-1}\), a standard second-order-cone constraint is \[(a^Tz+\alpha,Bz+b)\in\mathcal Q^m,\] equivalently \[\|Bz+b\|_2\le a^Tz+\alpha.\] This inequality also imposes \(a^Tz+\alpha\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A standard Lorentz-cone constraint bounds the Euclidean norm of a vector affine expression by a scalar affine expression and thereby requires the scalar expression to be nonnegative.
assumptions_latex: \(a\in\mathbb R^p\), \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{(m-1)\times p}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^{m-1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((t,x)\in\mathcal Q^m\iff\|x\|_2\le t\).

knowledge_statements.title: Standard–Rotated Cone Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact orthogonal conversion for the normalization \(2uv\ge\|w\|_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer \(m\ge2\), define \[T:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{m-2}\to\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{m-1},\qquad T(u,v,w)=\left(\frac{u+v}{\sqrt2},\frac{u-v}{\sqrt2},w\right).\] Then \[T(\mathcal Q_r^m)=\mathcal Q^m,\qquad (u,v,w)\in\mathcal Q_r^m\Longleftrightarrow T(u,v,w)\in\mathcal Q^m.\] The inverse conversion is \[T^{-1}(t,s,w)=\left(\frac{t+s}{\sqrt2},\frac{t-s}{\sqrt2},w\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orthogonal change of the first two coordinates converts rotated Lorentz-cone membership exactly into standard Lorentz-cone membership.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal Q^m\) uses the scalar-first convention \(\|(s,w)\|_2\le t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((u,v,w)\in\mathcal Q_r^m\iff T(u,v,w)\in\mathcal Q^m\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rotated second-order cone and standard-cone conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the rotated second-order cone and gives its orthogonal equivalence to a standard second-order cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(n\ge1\),
\[
\mathcal K_n^r=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^2:x^\top x\le2yz,\ y\ge0,\ z\ge0\}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
(x,y,z)\in\mathcal K_n^r
\iff
\left\|\begin{bmatrix}x\\(y-z)/\sqrt2\end{bmatrix}\right\|_2
\le \frac{y+z}{\sqrt2}.
\]
The corresponding change of variables is orthogonal, so \(\mathcal K_n^r\) is convex. Inequalities \(\|x\|_2^2\le2yz\) with \(y,z\ge0\) are called hyperbolic constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The rotated second-order cone is defined by ||x||₂² ≤ 2yz with y and z nonnegative. An orthogonal change of variables converts it exactly to a standard second-order cone, which also establishes convexity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x,y,z)\in\mathcal K_n^r\iff\left\|(x,(y-z)/\sqrt2)\right\|_2\le(y+z)/\sqrt2

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The low-dimensional Lorentz cones are polyhedral. The genuinely nonpolyhedral SOC regime begins at total dimension \(m=3\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Reduction Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact SOC reduction when all residual variation lies in a known lower-dimensional subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(t\in\mathbb R\). If \(Ax+b-c\in\operatorname{range}(U)\) for every \(x\in X\), then the SOC constraint has the exact reduced representation
\[(t,Ax+b-c)\in\mathcal Q^{m+1}\iff(t,U^{\mathsf T}(Ax+b-c))\in\mathcal Q^{r+1}.\]
Thus the two constraints define the same feasible pairs \((x,t)\in X\times\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When every possible residual lies in a known subspace with an orthonormal basis, its SOC constraint can be represented exactly using the coordinates in that basis.
assumptions_latex: \(m,n\in\mathbb N\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b,c\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall(x,t)\in X\times\mathbb R:\ (t,Ax+b-c)\in\mathcal Q^{m+1}\iff(t,U^{\mathsf T}(Ax+b-c))\in\mathcal Q^{r+1}\).

knowledge_statements.title: SOC Degeneracy Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between scalar, polyhedral low-dimensional, and genuinely second-order cone blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the convention
\[\mathcal Q^d=\{(t,u)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{d-1}:\|u\|_2\le t\},\]
the low-dimensional cases are
\[\mathcal Q^1=\mathbb R_+\]
and
\[\mathcal Q^2=\{(t,u)\in\mathbb R^2:t-u\ge0,\ t+u\ge0\}.\]
The cone \(\mathcal Q^d\) is nonpolyhedral for every integer \(d\ge3\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-dimensional Lorentz cone is a nonnegative ray, a two-dimensional Lorentz cone is polyhedral, and Lorentz cones of dimension at least three are nonpolyhedral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal Q^1=\mathbb R_+\), \(\mathcal Q^2=\{(t,u)\in\mathbb R^2:t-u\ge0,\ t+u\ge0\}\), and \(\mathcal Q^d\) is nonpolyhedral for every \(d\ge3\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard finite-dimensional conic representation of the Euclidean-norm epigraph, including the required coordinate permutation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(m\ge1\), the Euclidean-norm epigraph is
\[\operatorname{epi}\|\cdot\|_2=\{(z,t)\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R:\|z\|_2\le t\}.\]
For the coordinate permutation \(P(z,t)=(t,z)\),
\[P(\operatorname{epi}\|\cdot\|_2)=\mathcal Q^{m+1}.\]
Equivalently, \((z,t)\in\operatorname{epi}\|\cdot\|_2\) if and only if \((t,z)\in\mathcal Q^{m+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After swapping the vector and scalar coordinates, the epigraph of the Euclidean norm is exactly a Lorentz cone.
assumptions_latex: \(P:\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^m\) is defined by \(P(z,t)=(t,z)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(\operatorname{epi}\|\cdot\|_2)=\mathcal Q^{m+1}\), equivalently \((z,t)\in\operatorname{epi}\|\cdot\|_2\iff(t,z)\in\mathcal Q^{m+1}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

children.title: Least-Squares Models

knowledge_statements.title: Least-Squares Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SOC formulation preserving least-squares minimizers, although its objective value is the residual norm rather than its square.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[S=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\|Ax-b\|_2^2\]
and
\[T=\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,t)\in X\times\mathbb R}\{t:(t,Ax-b)\in\mathcal Q^{m+1}\}.\]
Then
\[S=\{x\in X:\exists t\in\mathbb R\text{ such that }(x,t)\in T\}.\]
If the optimal values are finite, the SOCP optimal value is the nonnegative square root of the least-squares optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Least squares and SOC residual-norm minimization have the same optimizing decisions after projecting away the SOC epigraph variable; their optimal values differ by squaring.
assumptions_latex: \(m,n\in\mathbb N\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty.
At least one of the two displayed optimization problems attains its optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\|Ax-b\|_2^2=\{x\in X:\exists t\in\mathbb R,\ (x,t)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{(y,s)\in X\times\mathbb R}\{s:(s,Ay-b)\in\mathcal Q^{m+1}\}\}\).

children.title: Weighted Residual Models
children.top_down_role: Residual formulations incorporating diagonal, block, or factor-based weighting.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Residual Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-semidefinite residual weighting, including singular weights and reduced SOC dimension through a thin factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x\in X\) and \(t\in\mathbb R\), the weighted-residual bound has the exact representation
\[\|Ax-b\|_Q\le t\iff(t,L(Ax-b))\in\mathcal Q^{r+1}.\]
Consequently,
\[\inf_{x\in X}\|Ax-b\|_Q=\inf_{(x,t)\in X\times\mathbb R}\{t:(t,L(Ax-b))\in\mathcal Q^{r+1}\}.\]
If \(Q\) is singular, residual components in \(\ker(Q)\) are unpenalized.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite weighted residual is represented as the Euclidean norm of a factored residual, with singular weights leaving their nullspace unpenalized.
assumptions_latex: \(m,n,r\in\mathbb N\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty.
\(Q\in\mathbb S_+^m\) and \(L\in\mathbb R^{r\times m}\) satisfy \(Q=L^{\mathsf T}L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall(x,t)\in X\times\mathbb R:\ \|Ax-b\|_Q\le t\iff(t,L(Ax-b))\in\mathcal Q^{r+1}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Minimax Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite Euclidean minimax model represented by a shared epigraph variable and multiple SOC blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Euclidean distance from the affine image \(Ax\) to the fixed point \(b\) is \(d(Ax,b)=\|Ax-b\|_2\). Its epigraph over \(X\) is
\[\{(x,t)\in X\times\mathbb R:(t,Ax-b)\in\mathcal Q^{m+1}\}.\]
Consequently, minimizing this distance is equivalent to minimizing \(t\) over that set. More generally, the bound \(d(Ax,b)\le\rho\) is represented by \((\rho,Ax-b)\in\mathcal Q^{m+1}\), which also enforces \(\rho\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distance from an affine image to a fixed point is an affine residual norm, so its epigraph or radius bound is one SOC constraint.

knowledge_statements.title: Worst-Case Distance Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario worst-case Euclidean distance, excluding general infinite uncertainty sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(D(x)=\max_{i\in I}\|x-a_i\|_2\),
\[D(x)\le t\iff(t,x-a_i)\in\mathcal Q^{n+1}\text{ for every }i\in I.\]
Consequently,
\[\inf_{x\in X}D(x)=\inf_{(x,t)\in X\times\mathbb R}\{t:(t,x-a_i)\in\mathcal Q^{n+1}\text{ for every }i\in I\}.\]
If the infimum is attained, the minimizing \(x\)-values are exactly the \(x\)-components of the conic minimizers. The formulation is an SOCP whenever \(X\) is SOCP-representable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many points, worst-case Euclidean distance is represented exactly by a common radius and one SOC constraint per point; optimizer correspondence holds when a solution exists.
assumptions_latex: \(k,n\in\mathbb N\), \(I=\{1,\ldots,k\}\), \(a_i\in\mathbb R^n\) for every \(i\in I\), and \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall(x,t)\in X\times\mathbb R:\ \max_{i\in I}\|x-a_i\|_2\le t\iff(t,x-a_i)\in\mathcal Q^{n+1}\ \forall i\in I\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A_i\in\mathbb R^{m_i\times n}\), and \(b_i\in\mathbb R^{m_i}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,k\). abla^2g=LL^T-hh^T\), where \(L\in\mathbb R^{l	imes(r-1)}\), \(r=\operatorname{rank}(

abla^2g\,\lambda=

children.title: Low-Rank Quadratic Models
children.top_down_role: SOC representations exploiting restricted rank in positive semidefinite quadratic data.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Quadratic Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-dimensional cone representation when the quadratic matrix has low rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\) have rank \(r\). There exists a full-row-rank \(R\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\) satisfying \(Q=R^{\mathsf T}R\). Consequently, \[x^{\mathsf T}Qx=\|Rx\|_2^2,\qquad t\ge x^{\mathsf T}Qx\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (t/2,1,Rx)\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm r}^{r+2}.\] The nonlinear conic block has dimension \(r+2\), determined by the rank rather than the ambient dimension \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-r PSD quadratic needs an r-dimensional factor image and a rotated cone of dimension r+2.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The epigraph of \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx\) admits a rotated-cone lift of dimension \(r+2\).

children.title: Factor-Form Quadratic Models
children.top_down_role: Quadratic models represented through explicit matrix factors and norm-compatible images.

knowledge_statements.title: Factor-Form Quadratic Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct SOC canonicalization of squared affine factor norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(f\in\mathbb R^m\), and let \(a^{\mathsf T}x+\beta\) be affine. The factor-form inequality \[\|Fx+f\|_2^2\le a^{\mathsf T}x+\beta\] is equivalent to \[\left(\frac{a^{\mathsf T}x+\beta}{2},1,Fx+f\right)\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm r}^{m+2}.\] Thus an explicit factor should be passed directly to the conic model; forming \(F^{\mathsf T}F\) is unnecessary for exact canonicalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A squared affine factor norm bounded by an affine expression is one rotated-cone constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|Fx+f\|_2^2\le a^{\mathsf T}x+\beta\) has the displayed exact rotated-SOC representation.

children.title: Rank-Deficient Factor Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Representation choices for noninjective or dimension-reducing quadratic factors.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ker Q=\ker R\), translations by \(\ker R\) preserve the quadratic value for every base point, and the rotated-cone epigraph remains exact without invertibility.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact behavior of quadratic models under a rank-deficient factor map.

source_refs.locator: 9.2 Geometry of linear and convex quadratic inequalities p. 296

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) be rank deficient and set \(Q=R^{\mathsf T}R\). Then \[x^{\mathsf T}Qx=\|Rx\|_2^2,\qquad \ker Q=\ker R.\] For every \(d\in\ker R\) and every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), the quadratic value at \(x+d\) equals its value at \(x\). Conversely, if a fixed direction \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) preserves the quadratic value for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), then \(d\in\ker R\). The epigraph remains exactly \[(t/2,1,Rx)\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm r}^{m+2}.\] No inverse of \(Q\) or \(R\) is required, and directions in \(\ker R\) are unpenalized.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank deficiency preserves exact factor-form canonicalization. Every nullspace direction preserves the quadratic value at all base points, and any direction with that global invariance lies in the nullspace.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Factor Interfaces

children.title: Factorization Sensitivity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural effects of factor choice, rank exposure, and numerical representation quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Sensitivity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation bound for fixed factors and non-Lipschitz behavior at rank loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(R,\widehat R\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \[\left|\|Rx\|_2^2-\|\widehat R x\|_2^2\right|\le(\|R\|_2+\|\widehat R\|_2)\|R-\widehat R\|_2\|x\|_2^2.\] However, the positive-semidefinite square-root map is not uniformly Lipschitz near rank loss: for scalar \(Q_\varepsilon=\varepsilon^2\) and \(Q_0=0\), \[\frac{|Q_\varepsilon^{1/2}-Q_0^{1/2}|}{|Q_\varepsilon-Q_0|}=\frac1\varepsilon\to\infty.\] Thus small matrix perturbations need not yield proportionally small factor perturbations near zero eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic values obey a factor perturbation bound, but square-root factors are not uniformly Lipschitz near rank loss.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) and \(\widehat R\) have the same dimensions.
\(\|\cdot\|_2\) denotes the spectral norm for matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Factor sensitivity can become unbounded as a positive eigenvalue approaches zero.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Both claims are mathematically plausible and the failure-boundary kind fits the container, but no source is supplied for either the perturbation inequality or the non-Lipschitz square-root boundary. A specific authoritative locator is required.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The epigraph is rotated-SOC representable and invariant under translations by \(\ker Q\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\) be singular, with rank \(r<n\), and choose \(R\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\) such that \(Q=R^{\mathsf T}R\). Then \[x^{\mathsf T}Qx=\|Rx\|_2^2,\qquad t\ge x^{\mathsf T}Qx\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (t/2,1,Rx)\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm r}^{r+2}.\] The epigraph is a cylinder along \(\ker Q\): if \(d\in\ker Q\), then \((x,t)\) is feasible exactly when \((x+d,t)\) is feasible. Invertibility is therefore unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular PSD quadratic has an exact reduced rotated-cone epigraph and is constant along its nullspace.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the rotated second-order cone by \(\mathcal Q_r^{n+2}=\{(u,v,z)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^n:u\geq0,\ v\geq0,\ 2uv\geq\|z\|_2^2\}\). For every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(t\in\mathbb R\), the squared-norm epigraph constraint has the exact conic representation \[t\geq\|x\|_2^2\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(t,1/2,x)\in\mathcal Q_r^{n+2}.\] More generally, if \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}\), \(y\in\mathbb R^d\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(t\in\mathbb R\), then \[t\geq\|Ay+b\|_2^2\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(t,1/2,Ay+b)\in\mathcal Q_r^{m+2}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A squared Euclidean norm is bounded by t exactly when t, one-half, and the norm argument form a rotated second-order-cone tuple.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-over-Linear Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-perspective formulation, including the finite boundary case at zero denominator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x,s)\) be the closed perspective of the squared norm, defined by \(q(x,s)=\|x\|_2^2/s\) when \(s>0\), \(q(0,0)=0\), and \(q(x,s)=+\infty\) otherwise. Then its epigraph is represented exactly by \[t\geq q(x,s)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (t,s/2,x)\in\mathcal Q_r^{n+2}.\] Thus the conic constraint imposes \(t\geq0\), \(s\geq0\), and \(ts\geq\|x\|_2^2\); at \(s=0\), it necessarily forces \(x=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed quadratic-over-linear epigraph is one rotated-cone constraint; at a zero denominator, only a zero numerator vector remains feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}q=\{(x,s,t):(t,s/2,x)\in\mathcal Q_r^{n+2}\}\)

children.title: Reciprocal Models
children.top_down_role: Rotated-SOC interfaces for reciprocal terms over admissible positive domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Reciprocal Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar positive reciprocal epigraph as a rotated-cone slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the extended-real reciprocal \(f(x)=1/x\) when \(x>0\) and \(f(x)=+\infty\) otherwise, its epigraph is \[\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb R^2:(t,x,\sqrt2)\in\mathcal Q_r^3\}.\] Indeed, membership in this rotated cone is precisely \(t\geq0\), \(x\geq0\), and \(tx\geq1\); the last inequality makes both scalar coordinates strictly positive and is equivalent to \(t\geq1/x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positive reciprocal epigraph is the rotated-cone slice obtained by fixing its vector coordinate to the square root of two.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\geq f(x)\iff(t,x,\sqrt2)\in\mathcal Q_r^3\)

children.title: Harmonic-Mean Models

knowledge_statements.title: Harmonic-Mean Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary harmonic mean modeled through the parallel-sum hypograph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(a,b>0\), let \(H_2(a,b)=2ab/(a+b)\). For a nonnegative hypograph variable \(h\), set \(p=h/2\). Then \[0\leq h\leq H_2(a,b)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (a-p,b-p,\sqrt2p)\in\mathcal Q_r^3,\qquad p=h/2.\] Equivalently, the cone enforces \(a-p\geq0\), \(b-p\geq0\), and \((a-p)(b-p)\geq p^2\), whose scalar inequality is \(p(a+b)\leq ab\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonnegative hypograph of the two-variable harmonic mean is one rotated-cone constraint after scaling the hypograph variable by one-half.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h\leq2ab/(a+b)\iff(a-h/2,b-h/2,h/\sqrt2)\in\mathcal Q_r^3\)

notation.meaning: Parallel-sum hypograph variable equal to half the harmonic-mean bound.

children.title: Reciprocal Domain Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Positivity, closure, and zero-boundary issues affecting reciprocal representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Reciprocal Domain Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary behavior of the closed positive-reciprocal model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=1/x\) for \(x>0\) and \(f(x)=+\infty\) for \(x\leq0\). No finite \(t\) satisfies \(t\geq f(0)\), and the rotated-cone slice \((t,x,\sqrt2)\in\mathcal Q_r^3\) likewise has no point with \(x=0\). Replacing the strict reciprocal domain by \(x\geq0\) while assigning a finite value at zero therefore changes the function and is not represented by this cone slice. Feasible sequences with \(x\downarrow0\) necessarily satisfy \(t\to+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positive reciprocal has no finite value at zero; any conic-feasible approach to zero forces the epigraph coordinate to diverge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\downarrow0\Longrightarrow t\geq1/x\to+\infty\)

knowledge_statements.title: Harmonic Aggregation Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive SOC interface for an unweighted harmonic mean of positive scalars.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x_i>0\), define \(P_n=(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^{-1})^{-1}\) and \(H_n=nP_n\). Set \(p_1=x_1\). For each \(k=2,\ldots,n\), impose \[(p_{k-1}-p_k,x_k-p_k,\sqrt2p_k)\in\mathcal Q_r^3.\] These constraints express \(0\leq p_k\leq(p_{k-1}^{-1}+x_k^{-1})^{-1}\). Consequently, for \(t\geq0\), \[t\leq H_n(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists p_2,\ldots,p_n\text{ satisfying the cone constraints and }t\leq np_n.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An n-variable harmonic-mean hypograph is assembled by recursively applying the binary parallel-sum rotated-cone interface and scaling the final output by n.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\leq n/(\sum_i x_i^{-1})\iff\exists(p_2,\ldots,p_n)\text{ satisfying the displayed SOC lift}\)

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric-Mean SOC Special Cases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-variable nonnegative geometric-mean hypograph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x,y,t\in\mathbb R\) with \(x\geq0\), \(y\geq0\), and \(t\geq0\), the geometric-mean hypograph is represented exactly by \[t\leq\sqrt{xy}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(x,y,\sqrt2t)\in\mathcal Q_r^3.\] Equivalently, the rotated cone imposes \(2xy\geq2t^2\). The ordinary second-order-cone form is \[\|(2t,x-y)\|_2\leq x+y,\] which is equivalent under the same nonnegativity conditions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\leq\sqrt{xy}\iff(x,y,\sqrt2t)\in\mathcal Q_r^3\iff\|(2t,x-y)\|_2\leq x+y\)

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k\in\mathbb Z_+\), \(m\in\{0,\ldots,2^k\}\), and \(\alpha=m/2^k\). Form a balanced binary tree with \(2^k\) leaves, assigning the value \(x\geq0\) to \(m\) leaves and the value \(1\) to the remaining leaves. At every internal node introduce a nonnegative value \(z\) and impose \((z_L,z_R,\sqrt2z)\in\mathcal Q_r^3\), where \(z_L\) and \(z_R\) are the values of its children. Let \(z_\rho\) denote the root value; when \(k=0\), the tree has one leaf and \(z_\rho\) is that leaf value, so there are no cone constraints. Then \[0\leq t\leq x^\alpha\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists\text{ internal-node values satisfying all cone constraints and }t\leq z_\rho.\]

children.title: Ellipsoid Representations
children.top_down_role: SOC-compatible descriptions of bounded affine images of Euclidean balls.

knowledge_statements.title: Ellipsoid Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine-image and SOC-lift representations, with the full-dimensional quadratic form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(c\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), the affine image of the unit ball is \[E=\{c+Au:u\in\mathbb R^r,\ \|u\|_2\leq1\}.\] Hence \(x\in E\) has the SOC lift \(x=c+Au\), \((1,u)\in\mathcal Q^{r+1}\). If \(A\) has full row rank and \(Q=AA^\mathsf T\succ0\), elimination of \(u\) gives the equivalent full-dimensional representation \[E=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:(x-c)^\mathsf TQ^{-1}(x-c)\leq1\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ellipsoid is an affine image of a Euclidean unit ball and therefore has an SOC lift; full-dimensional ellipsoids also have a positive-definite quadratic form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in E\iff\exists u:\ x=c+Au,\ \|u\|_2\leq1\)

notation.meaning: Shape matrix equal to the Gram matrix of A.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ellipsoid representations, degeneracy, and normalized volume
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines affine-image and quadratic representations of ellipsoids, distinguishes full-dimensional ellipsoids from the singular quadratic cylinder case, and records normalized-volume formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An ellipsoid in \(\mathbb{R}^n\) is a set \(E=\{Au+c:u\in\mathbb{R}^q,\ u^\top u\le 1\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times q}\). Every full-dimensional ellipsoid admits such a representation with \(q=n\) and \(A\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\), as well as a representation \(E=\{x:(x-c)^\top D(x-c)\le1\}\) with \(D=A^{-2}\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\). If \(D\succeq0\) is singular, the quadratic-inequality set is an elliptic cylinder whose unbounded directions form \(\ker D\). When volume is normalized so that the Euclidean unit ball has volume one, a full-dimensional ellipsoid satisfies \(\operatorname{Vol}(E)=\det A=(\det D)^{-1/2}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ellipsoid is an affine image of a Euclidean unit ball and may be lower-dimensional. A full-dimensional ellipsoid can be represented using a symmetric positive-definite affine shape matrix or an equivalent positive-definite quadratic inequality. A singular positive-semidefinite quadratic matrix instead gives an elliptic cylinder along its kernel. With unit-ball normalization, the volume is det(A), equivalently det(D)^(-1/2).
assumptions_latex: \text{For the full-dimensional representations and volume formulas, }q=n,\ A,D\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n,\ D=A^{-2}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E=\{Au+c:u^\top u\le1\}=\{x:(x-c)^\top D(x-c)\le1\},\qquad \operatorname{Vol}(E)=\det A=(\det D)^{-1/2}\text{ in the full-dimensional case}.

knowledge_statements.title: Ellipsoidal-Cylinder Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse affine images of a Euclidean ball under a rank-deficient map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and suppose \(C=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\|Ax-b\|_2\leq1\}\) is nonempty. Then \(C\) is SOC-representable by the single affine cone constraint \[(1,Ax-b)\in\mathcal Q^{m+1}.\] If \(\ker A\neq\{0\}\), the set is an ellipsoidal cylinder: for every \(x\in C\) and \(d\in\ker A\), one has \(x+\lambda d\in C\) for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\). If \(A\) is injective, this lineality disappears and \(C\) is bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inverse image of a Euclidean ball is one SOC constraint; a nontrivial kernel makes the represented set an unbounded ellipsoidal cylinder.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Ellipsoid Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singular shape matrices require an affine-hull constraint to define a bounded ellipsoid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\) be singular and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). The bounded degenerate ellipsoid generated by \(Q\) is \[E_Q=\{c+Q^{1/2}u:\|u\|_2\leq1\}=\{x:x-c\in\operatorname{range}Q,\ (x-c)^\mathsf TQ^\dagger(x-c)\leq1\}.\] The range condition is essential. If it is omitted, the set \(\{x:(x-c)^\mathsf TQ^\dagger(x-c)\leq1\}\) contains every translate along \(\ker Q\) and is an unbounded ellipsoidal cylinder rather than the lower-dimensional ellipsoid \(E_Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a singular shape matrix, the pseudoinverse inequality defines the intended bounded ellipsoid only when accompanied by its affine-hull range constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_Q=\{x:x-c\in\operatorname{range}Q,\ (x-c)^\mathsf TQ^\dagger(x-c)\leq1\}\)
