knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Arrow Condensation Can Be Dense
Condensation Sparsity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fill-in created when sparse equality variables are eliminated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a sparse linear system have bipartite incidence graph between equations and variables. Eliminating a variable \(y_j\) by substitution couples every pair of remaining equations or variables adjacent through \(y_j\); graphically, its remaining neighbors are completed to a clique. Hence condensation preserves a prescribed sparsity pattern only when every fill edge induced by the elimination order already belongs to that pattern. A sparse original model may therefore produce a dense condensed model when an eliminated block has many mutually nonadjacent neighbors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elimination creates clique fill among the eliminated block’s neighbors; sparsity is preserved only when all induced fill edges are already present.
assumptions_latex: The model is represented by the nonzero pattern of its linear equality coefficients.
Elimination uses exact algebraic substitution without auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Condensation can increase nonzeros by all fill edges generated by the chosen elimination order.

knowledge_statements.title: Factorization-Based SOC Routes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order-cone representation of a positive-semidefinite quadratic inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and choose any factor \(R\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\) satisfying \(Q=R^{\mathsf T}R\). Then, for \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(t\in\mathbb R\),
\[x^{\mathsf T}Qx\le t^2,\quad t\ge0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\|Rx\|_2\le t
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(t,Rx)\in\mathcal Q^{r+1}.\]
Thus a convex quadratic bound is represented exactly by one second-order-cone constraint after a Cholesky, spectral, or other Gram factorization of \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factoring a positive-semidefinite quadratic form converts its nonnegative quadratic bound exactly into a second-order-cone constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx\le t^2\) if and only if \((t,Rx)\in\mathcal Q^{r+1}\).

notation.meaning: Cone of real positive-semidefinite symmetric matrices.
Gram factor of the quadratic matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsingular Schur-Complement Routes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical Schur-complement equivalence with a positive-definite pivot block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb S^p\), \(C\in\mathbb S_{++}^q\), and \(B\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}\). Then
\[\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^{\mathsf T}&C\end{pmatrix}\succeq0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
A-BC^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}\succeq0.\]
Equivalently, a matrix-fractional inequality \(A\succeq BC^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}\) can be replaced exactly by the displayed linear matrix inequality whenever the pivot matrix \(C\) is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a positive-definite pivot, a block positive-semidefinite constraint is exactly equivalent to positivity of its ordinary Schur complement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^{\mathsf T}&C\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\) if and only if \(A-BC^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Positive-definite symmetric matrices of order q.
Inverse of the positive-definite pivot block.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-definite Schur-complement equivalence is standard, precise, and correctly classified as a representation, but the record supplies no citation or inspectable locator.

children.title: Generalized Schur Routes
children.top_down_role: Schur-type reformulation routes extending beyond ordinary invertible principal blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Schur Routes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized Schur-complement theorem for a positive-semidefinite, possibly singular pivot.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb S^p\), \(C\in\mathbb S_+^q\), and \(B\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}\). With \(C^\dagger\) denoting the Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse,
\[\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^{\mathsf T}&C\end{pmatrix}\succeq0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
C\succeq0,\quad (I-CC^\dagger)B^{\mathsf T}=0,\quad A-BC^\dagger B^{\mathsf T}\succeq0.\]
The middle equality is the range-compatibility condition and cannot in general be omitted when \(C\) is singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a singular positive-semidefinite pivot, block positivity requires both a pseudoinverse Schur inequality and compatibility of the off-diagonal block with the pivot range.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Block positive semidefiniteness is equivalent to range compatibility and \(A-BC^\dagger B^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the nullspace of the pivot.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generalized Schur theorem includes the necessary pseudoinverse and range condition and fits the route leaf, but no source with a theorem, section, or page locator is supplied.

children.title: Singular Schur Routes
children.top_down_role: Matrix reformulation routes involving singular or rank-deficient principal blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Schur Routes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph LMI obtained from a singular quadratic form using its pseudoinverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), possibly singular, and let \(z\in\mathbb R^n\), \(t\in\mathbb R\). Then
\[\begin{pmatrix}t&z^{\mathsf T}\\z&Q\end{pmatrix}\succeq0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
z\in\operatorname{range}(Q),\qquad t\ge z^{\mathsf T}Q^\dagger z.\]
Thus the block LMI is an exact conic route for the pseudoinverse quadratic epigraph only on the range-compatible domain; outside that domain its left-hand side is infeasible for every finite \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular quadratic epigraph has an exact block-LMI representation only when its vector lies in the quadratic matrix’s range.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The block LMI is equivalent to \(z\in\operatorname{range}(Q)\) and \(t\ge z^{\mathsf T}Q^\dagger z\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The singular-pivot epigraph representation is mathematically consistent and correctly includes range compatibility, but it has no supporting citation or locator.

children.title: Range-Compatibility Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Structural compatibility between off-diagonal data and singular block ranges.

knowledge_statements.title: Range-Compatibility Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent predicates ensuring compatibility with a singular Schur pivot.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(C\in\mathbb S_+^q\) and \(B\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}\), the range-compatibility interface for a Schur route is
\[\operatorname{range}(B^{\mathsf T})\subseteq\operatorname{range}(C).\]
It admits the equivalent algebraic forms
\[(I-CC^\dagger)B^{\mathsf T}=0,
\qquad
\ker(C)\subseteq\ker(B).\]
Any of these predicates is necessary for positive semidefiniteness of \(\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^{\mathsf T}&C\end{pmatrix}\), independently of the value of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatibility means the off-diagonal block’s columns lie in the singular pivot’s range; projector and nullspace tests express the same condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{range}(B^{\mathsf T})\subseteq\operatorname{range}(C)\), \((I-CC^\dagger)B^{\mathsf T}=0\), and \(\ker(C)\subseteq\ker(B)\) are equivalent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The range, projector, and kernel predicates are dimensionally consistent and equivalent, and condition is the correct content kind. An inspectable source locator is nevertheless required.

children.title: Singular-Route Exactness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions separating exact singular reformulations from weakened or invalid representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Route Exactness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure caused by omitting range compatibility from a singular Schur route.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Take
\[Q=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad z=\begin{pmatrix}0\\1\end{pmatrix}.\]
Then \(Q^\dagger=Q\), so the pseudoinverse inequality \(t\ge z^{\mathsf T}Q^\dagger z\) reduces to \(t\ge0\). Nevertheless \(z\notin\operatorname{range}(Q)\), and
\[\begin{pmatrix}t&z^{\mathsf T}\\z&Q\end{pmatrix}\not\succeq0\]
for every \(t\in\mathbb R\). Hence the pseudoinverse inequality alone is not an exact replacement for a singular-pivot block LMI.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular pseudoinverse inequality may hold while the corresponding block LMI is infeasible because the vector violates range compatibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Range compatibility is indispensable for exactness of the singular Schur reformulation.

notation.meaning: Off-diagonal vector outside the range of Q.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The example correctly demonstrates failure when range compatibility is omitted and counterexample fits the exactness-boundary leaf, but no source or locator supports the record.

knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Exactness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between inverse-based and pseudoinverse-based Schur reformulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a symmetric block matrix \(M=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^{\mathsf T}&C\end{pmatrix}\), the inverse-based equivalence \(M\succeq0\Longleftrightarrow A-BC^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\) is exact only when \(C\succ0\). If \(C\succeq0\) is singular, exactness requires replacing \(C^{-1}\) by \(C^\dagger\) and adding \(\operatorname{range}(B^{\mathsf T})\subseteq\operatorname{range}(C)\). If \(C\) has a negative eigenvalue, then \(M\succeq0\) is impossible because every principal submatrix of a positive-semidefinite matrix is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordinary Schur exactness requires a positive-definite pivot; singular pivots need a pseudoinverse plus range compatibility, while indefinite pivots preclude block positivity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pivot regimes \(C\succ0\), singular \(C\succeq0\), and \(C\not\succeq0\) require distinct exactness conditions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The three pivot regimes accurately describe the boundary of the PSD Schur-complement reformulation and failure_boundary is the correct role, but the record contains no citation or locator.

knowledge_statements.title: SOC-to-PSD Embeddings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact semidefinite embedding of the Lorentz cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n\ge1\), \(t\in\mathbb R\), and \(x\in\mathbb R^n\). Membership in the Lorentz cone has the exact semidefinite representation
\[(t,x)\in\mathcal Q^{n+1}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\|x\|_2\le t
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\begin{pmatrix}t&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&tI_n\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lorentz-cone constraint is exactly equivalent to positive semidefiniteness of a structured arrow matrix, yielding a direct SOC-to-PSD embedding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((t,x)\in\mathcal Q^{n+1}\) if and only if \(\begin{pmatrix}t&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&tI_n\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\).

source_refs.locator: 11.1 From linear to conic models p. 381

source_witnesses.locator: 11.1 From linear to conic models p. 381

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral and Rank Structure of the Arrow Embedding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral characterization of the standard Lorentz-to-PSD arrow embedding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M(t,x)=\begin{pmatrix}t&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&tI_n\end{pmatrix}\), the eigenvalues are \(t+\|x\|_2\), \(t-\|x\|_2\), and \(t\) with multiplicity \(n-1\). Hence \(M(t,x)\succ0\) iff \(t>\|x\|_2\). If \(x\ne0\) and \(t=\|x\|_2\), then \(M(t,x)\) has rank \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit eigenvalues identify strict Lorentz-cone membership and the nonzero boundary rank of the arrow embedding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{spec}M(t,x)=\{t+\|x\|_2,t-\|x\|_2,t\text{ with multiplicity }n-1\}\).

notation.meaning: Arrow matrix used in the SOC-to-PSD embedding.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral and Rank Structure of the Arrow Embedding
PSD Models with SOC Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact SOC representation of arrow-structured positive-semidefinite constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer \(n\ge 1\), scalar \(t\in\mathbb R\), and vector \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), define \(M(t,x)=\begin{pmatrix}t&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&tI_n\end{pmatrix}\). Then \[M(t,x)\succeq0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \|x\|_2\le t.\] Consequently, replacing every constraint \(M(t,x)\succeq0\) by \((t,x)\in\mathcal Q^{n+1}\), where \(\mathcal Q^{n+1}=\{(s,u):\|u\|_2\le s\}\), preserves the feasible set and objective values. A block-diagonal PSD constraint whose blocks all have this arrow form therefore has an exact product-of-SOC representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An arrow-shaped PSD constraint is equivalent to one second-order-cone constraint; products of such blocks can be converted exactly to SOC form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M(t,x)\succeq0\Longleftrightarrow(t,x)\in\mathcal Q^{n+1}\).

source_refs.locator: 11.1 From linear to conic models p. 381

source_witnesses.locator: 11.1 From linear to conic models p. 381

knowledge_statements.statement_title: General PSD Cones of Order at Least Three Have No Finite SOC Lift
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary showing that exact finite SOC conversion of PSD constraints requires special affine or block structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every integer \(n\ge3\), the cone \(\mathbb S_+^n\) is not the linear image of an affine slice of any finite Cartesian product of Lorentz cones. Thus a general positive-semidefinite constraint of order at least three has no exact finite second-order-cone lift, although special structured slices and products of blocks of order at most two can be SOC representable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general PSD cone of order at least three has no finite SOC lift, so exact PSD-to-SOC conversion depends on special structure.
assumptions_latex: Only finite-dimensional affine lifts over finite products of Lorentz cones are allowed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb S_+^n\) is not finitely second-order-cone representable for \(n\ge3\).

notation.meaning: Cone of real symmetric positive-semidefinite matrices of order n.

knowledge_statements.title: General PSD Cones of Order at Least Three Have No Finite SOC Lift

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Two-by-Two PSD Blocks as Rotated Cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rotated-SOC representation of an arbitrary real symmetric two-by-two PSD block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(a,b,c\in\mathbb R\),
\[\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{pmatrix}\succeq0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
a\ge0,\ c\ge0,\ ac\ge b^2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(a,c,\sqrt2 b)\in\mathcal Q_r^3,\]
where \(\mathcal Q_r^3=\{(u,v,w):u\ge0,\ v\ge0,\ 2uv\ge w^2\}\). Consequently, a block-diagonal PSD constraint whose blocks have order at most two has an exact product-of-rotated-SOC representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every real symmetric two-by-two PSD constraint is exactly one rotated second-order-cone constraint, and products of such blocks are SOCP representable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\Longleftrightarrow(a,c,\sqrt2 b)\in\mathcal Q_r^3\).
knowledge_statements.title: Two-by-Two PSD Blocks as Rotated Cones

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equal Values Need Not Preserve Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp distinction between equality of optimal values and optimizer existence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The problem \(P=\min\{x^2:x\in\mathbb R\}\) has value \(0\), attained at \(x=0\). The problem \(R=\inf\{z:z>0\}\) also has value \(0\), but has no minimizer. Thus the two problems have equal infima although attainment is not preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two problems can have the same infimum even though only one attains it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{val}(P)=\operatorname{val}(R)=0\), while \(\operatorname*{argmin}P=\{0\}\) and \(\operatorname*{argmin}R=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Equal Values Need Not Preserve Attainment

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Value Preservation Is an Equivalence Relation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic structure of equality of extended-real optimal values for a fixed objective sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For optimization problems with a common objective sense, define \(P\sim R\) when their extended-real optimal values are equal. Then \(\sim\) is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive. Consequently, any finite chain of value-preserving reformulations is value-preserving from its first problem to its last.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality of optimal values makes value preservation reflexive, symmetric, transitive, and compositional.
assumptions_latex: All compared problems use the same minimization or maximization convention.
Optimal values are interpreted in \(\overline{\mathbb R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\sim P\), \(P\sim R\Rightarrow R\sim P\), and \(P\sim R\land R\sim S\Rightarrow P\sim S\).
knowledge_statements.title: Value Preservation Is an Equivalence Relation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational equivalent of value preservation for nonempty minimization problems with finite values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\) and \(r=\inf_{z\in G}g(z)\), where \(F,G\ne\varnothing\) and \(p,r\in\mathbb R\). Then \(p=r\) if and only if, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), both conditions hold: for every \(x\in F\) there exists \(z\in G\) such that \(g(z)\le f(x)+\varepsilon\), and for every \(z\in G\) there exists \(x\in F\) such that \(f(x)\le g(z)+\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finite nonempty minimization problems, equal infima are equivalent to approximate objective transfer in both directions.
assumptions_latex: Both infima are finite real numbers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=r\iff\) bidirectional \(\varepsilon\)-objective transfer holds for every \(\varepsilon>0\).
review_flags: The characterization requires modification for empty feasible sets or infinite optimal values.
knowledge_statements.title: Epsilon-Objective Transfer Characterization
Value-Preserving Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality of extended-real optimal values, without requiring optimizer correspondence or attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) and \(R\) be minimization problems with feasible sets \(F\) and \(G\) and objectives \(f:F\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) and \(g:G\to\overline{\mathbb R}\). The passage from \(P\) to \(R\) is value-preserving when \[\inf_{x\in F}f(x)=\inf_{z\in G}g(z)\] in \(\overline{\mathbb R}\). This condition alone neither asserts that either infimum is attained nor supplies a map between feasible or optimal solutions. For maximization problems, the corresponding definition uses equality of suprema.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reformulation is value-preserving when its optimal extended-real value equals that of the original problem, regardless of attainment or solution recovery.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(G\) are the respective feasible sets.
\(f:F\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) and \(g:G\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) are minimization objectives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in F}f(x)=\inf_{z\in G}g(z)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically precise and correctly distinguishes value preservation from attainment and recovery, but no inspectable citation is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical recovery certificate for an exact auxiliary-variable lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\subseteq X\times Y\) satisfy \(\pi_X(G)=F\), and let \(g(x,y)=f(x)\). If the lifted problem attains its minimum, then projection \(\rho(x,y)=x\) maps every lifted optimizer to an original optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an exact lift whose objective depends only on original variables, discarding auxiliaries recovers an original optimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_X(\operatorname{argmin}_G g)\subseteq\operatorname{argmin}_F f\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Projection Recovery Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recovery of original optimizers from attained reformulated optimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\) and \(R=\inf_{z\in G}g(z)\) attain a common finite value \(v\). The reformulation is solution-recoverable for \(P\) if a specified map \(\rho:\operatorname{argmin}_G g\to F\) satisfies \(\rho(z)\in\operatorname{argmin}_F f\) and \(f(\rho(z))=g(z)=v\) for every reformulated optimizer \(z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every reformulated optimizer is mapped by a specified rule to an original optimizer with the same value.
assumptions_latex: Both problems attain a common finite value \(v\).
The recovery claim covers every reformulated optimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(\operatorname{argmin}_G g)\subseteq\operatorname{argmin}_F f\).
knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Recoverable Reformulation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Composition and Nonattainment Boundary for Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transitivity of recovery and its sharp optimizer-existence boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(R_2\) is solution-recoverable for \(R_1\) by \(\rho_{21}\) and \(R_1\) is solution-recoverable for \(P\) by \(\rho_{10}\), then \(R_2\) is solution-recoverable for \(P\) by \(\rho_{10}\circ\rho_{21}\). Conversely, under the optimizer-based definition, a value-preserving reformulation with empty argmin is not solution-recoverable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recovery maps compose, while a reformulation having no optimizer cannot support optimizer-based recovery.
assumptions_latex: Each recovery map is defined for every optimizer covered by its claim.
For the negative case, the original problem attains while the reformulation has empty argmin.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{10}\circ\rho_{21}\) is a recovery map; nonattainment violates the definition's attainment requirement.
knowledge_statements.title: Composition and Nonattainment Boundary for Recovery
Solution-Recoverable Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recovery of original optimizers from optimizers of a reformulated problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\) and \(R=\inf_{z\in G}g(z)\), and suppose both problems attain a common finite value \(v\). The reformulation \(R\) is solution-recoverable for \(P\) if a specified map \(\rho:\operatorname{argmin}_{G}g\to F\) satisfies \[\rho(z)\in\operatorname{argmin}_{F}f\quad\text{and}\quad f(\rho(z))=g(z)=v\] for every \(z\in\operatorname{argmin}_{G}g\). Recovery may discard auxiliary variables, but it must be defined for every reformulated optimizer covered by the claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every optimizer of a solution-recoverable reformulation can be mapped by a specified rule to an optimizer of the original problem with the same value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(\operatorname{argmin}_{G}g)\subseteq\operatorname{argmin}_{F}f\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The optimizer-recovery definition fits the leaf and is internally consistent, but it has no source or locator supporting this particular recovery convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Outer Conic Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic supersets that provide lower bounds for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the feasible set of a minimization problem and let \(F_{\mathrm{out}}\) be conic representable. It is an outer conic relaxation when \(F\subseteq F_{\mathrm{out}}\). For every objective \(f:F_{\mathrm{out}}\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), \[\inf_{x\in F_{\mathrm{out}}}f(x)\le\inf_{x\in F}f(x).\] If a nested family satisfies \(F\subseteq F_{k+1}\subseteq F_k\), then its relaxation values are nondecreasing lower bounds. Equality or convergence requires additional exactness or approximation hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An outer conic relaxation enlarges the feasible set, producing a lower bound for minimization; nested tightening yields nondecreasing bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in F_{\mathrm{out}}}f(x)\le\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Outer conic approximation of the feasible set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness certificate when an attained outer-relaxation optimizer is originally feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq F_{\mathrm{out}}\), and let \(x_{\mathrm{out}}\in\operatorname{argmin}_{F_{\mathrm{out}}}f\cap F\). Then \(x_{\mathrm{out}}\in\operatorname{argmin}_F f\) and \(\min_{F_{\mathrm{out}}}f=\min_F f=f(x_{\mathrm{out}})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxed optimizer satisfying the original constraints certifies relaxation exactness and original optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{\mathrm{out}}\in\operatorname{argmin}_F f\) and \(\min_{F_{\mathrm{out}}}f=\min_F f\).
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Relaxation Optimizer Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Value with Spurious Relaxed Optimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of optimizer recovery despite equality of original and relaxed values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F=\{0\}\), \(F_{\mathrm{out}}=[0,1]\), and \(f\equiv0\), one has \(\min_{F_{\mathrm{out}}}f=\min_F f=0\), but every \(x\in(0,1]\) is a relaxed optimizer infeasible for the original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An outer relaxation can have the exact value while retaining spurious optimal solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{argmin}_{F_{\mathrm{out}}}f\not\subseteq F\) despite equality of optimal values.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Value with Spurious Relaxed Optimizers
Inner Conic Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic subsets that provide feasible upper bounds for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the feasible set of a minimization problem and let \(F_{\mathrm{in}}\) be conic representable. It is an inner conic approximation when \(F_{\mathrm{in}}\subseteq F\). For every objective \(f:F\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), \[\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\le\inf_{x\in F_{\mathrm{in}}}f(x).\] Every point feasible for the inner problem is feasible for the original problem. If \(F_k\subseteq F_{k+1}\subseteq F\), the corresponding minimization values are nonincreasing upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inner conic approximation restricts the feasible set, producing feasible solutions and an upper bound for minimization; nested expansion improves the bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\le\inf_{x\in F_{\mathrm{in}}}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Inner conic approximation of the feasible set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certification of original optimality by matching an inner-feasible value to a valid lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_{\mathrm{in}}\subseteq F\), \(x_{\mathrm{in}}\in F_{\mathrm{in}}\), and \(L\le\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\). If \(f(x_{\mathrm{in}})=L\), then \(x_{\mathrm{in}}\in\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\) and \(\inf_F f=\inf_{F_{\mathrm{in}}}f=L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inner-feasible point is globally optimal when its value equals a valid lower bound for the original problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{\mathrm{in}}\in\operatorname{argmin}_F f\) and \(\inf_F f=\inf_{F_{\mathrm{in}}}f=L\).

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound on the original minimization value.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner-Approximation Optimality Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective Exactness Does Not Imply Set Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the converse from equality of one objective value to equality of feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F=[0,1]\), \(F_{\mathrm{in}}=\{0\}\), and \(f(x)=x\), one has \(F_{\mathrm{in}}\subsetneq F\) but \(\min_{F_{\mathrm{in}}}f=\min_F f=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper inner approximation can be exact for a particular objective without exactly representing the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_{\mathrm{in}}\subsetneq F\) while \(\min_{F_{\mathrm{in}}}f=\min_F f\).
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Exactness Does Not Imply Set Exactness

children.title: Closure Changes under Reformulation
children.top_down_role: Changes in feasible-set or value-set closedness induced by lifting, projection, or representation replacement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional sufficient condition for projection to preserve closedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\) be closed. Suppose that for every sequence \(x_k\in\pi_x(S)\) converging to \(\bar x\), lifts \((x_k,y_k)\in S\) can be chosen so that \(\{y_k\}\) has a bounded subsequence. Then \(\pi_x(S)\) is closed. In particular, this holds when \(\pi_x|_S\) is proper.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection preserves closedness when convergent projected sequences admit nonescaping lifts; proper projections satisfy this condition.
assumptions_latex: Every convergent sequence in \(\pi_x(S)\) admits lifts with a bounded subsequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_x(S)\) is closed.

notation.meaning: Projection restricted to the lifted feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonescaping-Lift Criterion for Closed Projection

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed Conic Slice with Nonclosed Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit failure of closedness preservation under projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\{(x,y):(x,y,\sqrt2)\in\mathcal Q_r^3\}\), where \(\mathcal Q_r^3=\{(x,y,z):2xy\ge z^2,\ x,y\ge0\}\). Then \(S\) is closed and \(\pi_x(S)=(0,\infty)\), because a lift exists exactly when \(x>0\), with \(y\ge1/x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed rotated-cone slice can project to an open ray.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\) is closed but \(\pi_x(S)=(0,\infty)\) is not closed.
knowledge_statements.title: Closed Conic Slice with Nonclosed Projection

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation class immune to projection-induced nonclosedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+m}\) is a polyhedron, then \(\pi_x(S)\) is a polyhedron and therefore is closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating variables from a finite linear-inequality system cannot create a nonclosed projected feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_x(S)\) is a closed polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Projections Remain Closed
Closure Changes under Reformulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection of a closed conic feasible set need not remain closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Q_r^3=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:2xy\ge z^2,\ x\ge0,\ y\ge0\}\) be the rotated second-order cone and define the closed convex slice \(S=\{(x,y):(x,y,\sqrt2)\in\mathcal Q_r^3\}\). Its projection onto the first coordinate is \[\pi_x(S)=\{x\in\mathbb R:x>0\},\] because a lift exists exactly when \(x>0\), with some \(y\ge1/x\). Hence \(S\) is closed while \(\pi_x(S)\) is not; eliminating conic lifting variables can therefore change closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed rotated-cone slice can project to the open ray, so eliminating auxiliary conic variables need not preserve closedness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\) is closed but \(\pi_x(S)=(0,\infty)\) is not closed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rotated-cone projection example is mathematically coherent and the failure-boundary role fits, but the nonclosed-projection claim has no cited source or locator.

children.title: Attainment Changes under Reformulation
children.top_down_role: Changes in existence of optimizing representatives after reformulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closure Equivalence Does Not Preserve Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment may differ when projected feasible sets agree only after closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\min\{x:x\ge0\}\) and \(R=\inf\{x:(x,y,\sqrt2)\in\mathcal Q_r^3\}\), where \(\mathcal Q_r^3=\{(x,y,z):2xy\ge z^2,\ x,y\ge0\}\). The projection of the feasible set of \(R\) is \((0,\infty)\), whose closure is the feasible set of \(P\). Both values are \(0\), but only \(P\) attains it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closure-equivalent descriptions can have the same infimum but different attainment status.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min P=\inf R=0\), while \(P\) attains and \(R\) does not.
knowledge_statements.title: Closure Equivalence Does Not Preserve Attainment

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Attainment Invariance under an Exact Surjective Reformulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient condition preventing attainment changes under reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho:G\to F\) be surjective and satisfy \(g(z)=f(\rho(z))\) for all \(z\in G\). Then \(\inf_G g=\inf_F f\), \(\operatorname{argmin}_G g=\rho^{-1}(\operatorname{argmin}_F f)\), and one problem attains its infimum if and only if the other does.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A surjective feasible-point map preserving objective values preserves optimal value and attainment in both directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{argmin}_G g=\rho^{-1}(\operatorname{argmin}_F f)\), so attainment is invariant.

notation.meaning: Feasible-point map from reformulated to original variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Attainment Invariance under an Exact Surjective Reformulation
Attainment Changes under Reformulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure-equivalent feasible descriptions may differ in attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(P=\min\{x:x\ge0\}\) and the lifted conic problem \(R=\inf\{x:(x,y,\sqrt2)\in\mathcal Q_r^3\}\). The projected feasible set of \(R\) is \((0,\infty)\), whose closure is the feasible set \([0,\infty)\) of \(P\). Both optimal values equal \(0\), but \(P\) attains its value at \(x=0\), whereas \(R\) has no minimizer because every lifted feasible point has \(x>0\). Thus closure replacement can preserve value while changing attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closure-based conic reformulation may keep the infimum but lose an optimizer, even when its projected feasible set is dense in the original set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min P=\inf R=0\), while \(P\) attains and \(R\) does not.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The example correctly exhibits equal infima with attainment only in the closed original problem, but no inspectable source supports the example or its reformulation interpretation.

children.title: Infimum-Preserving Nonattainment
children.top_down_role: Reformulations preserving optimal value while altering solution attainment.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional attainment condition ruling out the pathology.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:G\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be lower semicontinuous with \(v=\inf_G g\in\mathbb R\). If \(\{z\in G:g(z)\le\alpha\}\) is nonempty and compact for some \(\alpha>v\), then \(g\) attains \(v\). Moreover, if \(g\) is lower semicontinuous and does not attain \(v\), no minimizing sequence has a cluster point in \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower semicontinuity and one compact lower level set force attainment; without attainment, minimizing sequences have no feasible cluster point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{g\le\alpha\}\text{ compact for some }\alpha>v\Rightarrow\operatorname{argmin}_G g\ne\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Level strictly above the finite infimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Compact Lower-Level Sets Exclude Nonattainment

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value preservation when the reformulated problem has no optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an original problem attain the finite value \(v\). A reformulated problem \(\inf_{z\in G}g(z)\) exhibits infimum-preserving nonattainment when \(\inf_G g=v\) and \(\operatorname{argmin}_G g=\varnothing\). Equivalently, for every \(\varepsilon>0\) some \(z_\varepsilon\in G\) satisfies \(g(z_\varepsilon)\le v+\varepsilon\), while no feasible \(z\) satisfies \(g(z)=v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reformulation preserves the finite infimum but has only arbitrarily accurate minimizing points, not an optimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_G g=v\) and \(\operatorname{argmin}_G g=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Infimum-Preserving Nonattainment Criterion
Infimum-Preserving Nonattainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value preservation when the reformulated problem has no optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\min_{x\in F}f(x)\) attain a finite value \(v\), and let \(R=\inf_{z\in G}g(z)\) be a reformulation. The reformulation exhibits infimum-preserving nonattainment when \[\inf_{z\in G}g(z)=v\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname{argmin}_{G}g=\varnothing.\] Equivalently, for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there exists \(z_\varepsilon\in G\) with \(g(z_\varepsilon)\le v+\varepsilon\), but no feasible \(z\in G\) satisfies \(g(z)=v\). Value preservation therefore does not imply optimizer preservation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reformulated problem has the same finite infimum as the original attained problem but only admits arbitrarily accurate minimizing sequences, not an optimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{z\in G}g(z)=v\) and \(\operatorname{argmin}_{G}g=\varnothing\).

children.title: Closure–Recovery Mismatches
children.top_down_role: Cases where closure operations disrupt recovery of solutions for the original representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected closure points need not possess representatives in the closed lifted set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq X\times Y\) be closed and \(F=\pi_X(S)\). For every \(\bar x\in\operatorname{cl}F\setminus F\), one has \(\{y\in Y:(\bar x,y)\in S\}=\varnothing\). Thus closing the projection adds points for which no feasible lift, and hence no lift-based recovery, exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A newly added closure point of a projection has no feasible auxiliary representative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{y\in Y:(\bar x,y)\in S\}=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Closure Points without Recoverable Lifts

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential characterization of recovery at projected limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\) be closed and let \((x_k,y_k)\in S\) with \(x_k\to\bar x\). If \(\{y_k\}\) has a bounded subsequence, then \(\bar x\) has a feasible lift. Consequently, if \(\bar x\in\operatorname{cl}\pi_x(S)\setminus\pi_x(S)\), every such lift sequence has no bounded subsequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded auxiliary representatives yield recovery at a limit; unrecoverable closure points force all representatives to escape.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{y_k\}\text{ has a bounded subsequence}\Rightarrow\exists\bar y:(\bar x,\bar y)\in S\).

notation.meaning: Auxiliary representatives of projected feasible points.

knowledge_statements.title: Compact Recovery versus Lift Escape
Closure–Recovery Mismatches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit points of projected lifts may lack recoverable lifted solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq X\times Y\) be a closed lifted feasible set and \(F=\pi_X(S)\). If \(F\ne\operatorname{cl}F\), then any point \(\bar x\in\operatorname{cl}F\setminus F\) is approached by projected feasible points but has no lift \(\bar y\) satisfying \((\bar x,\bar y)\in S\). Therefore a recovery rule that must return a feasible lift cannot be extended to \(\bar x\). For the rotated-cone slice \(S=\{(x,y):(x,y,\sqrt2)\in\mathcal Q_r^3\}\), the limit point \(\bar x=0\) has no recoverable \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closing a projected feasible set can add limit points with no feasible lift, so value limits need not support solution recovery.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{y\in Y:(\bar x,y)\in S\}=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Closure of the projected feasible set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection argument correctly identifies closure points without lifts and fits the failure-boundary container, but neither the general claim nor the rotated-cone instance has an inspectable citation.
