knowledge_statements.title: Expression Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-preserving normalization of an expression DAG before conic graph expansion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an expression DAG \(E\), initialize \(E_0=E\). Repeatedly replace any eligible node by a deterministic canonical form using constant folding, affine-term collection, sign normalization, argument ordering for commutative atoms, and elimination of identity operations. A rewrite \(u\mapsto v\) is admissible only when \(\operatorname{dom}u=\operatorname{dom}v\), \(u(x)=v(x)\) on that domain, and the recorded shape, sign, and curvature attributes remain valid. Stop when no rule applies; output the resulting DAG \(N(E)\). Thus \(N(E)(x)=E(x)\) for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply deterministic local rewrites until none remains, preserving the expression’s domain, value, dimensions, sign information, and certified curvature.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite, acyclic, well-typed expression graph.
Every rewrite rule has a verified value-and-domain preservation contract.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N(E)\) is canonical relative to the rule system and satisfies \(N(E)(x)=E(x)\) on \(\operatorname{dom}E\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: deterministic semantics-preserving rewriting is a standard canonicalization invariant
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf and is internally coherent, but no inspectable source supports the stated normalization rules, attribute-preservation contract, termination behavior, or canonical-form claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinearity Linearization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conic lifting of supported nonlinear atoms, not numerical first-order approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a supported convex atom \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) possess a conic graph template. Its epigraph constraint is represented by auxiliary variables \(z\in\mathbb{R}^q\) and affine data through \[f(x)\le t\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists z:\ A x+B t+C z+d\in K.\] For a supported concave atom, an analogous hypograph template represents \(t\le f(x)\). Substitution replaces the nonlinear relation by affine expressions and membership in a product cone. The lift is exact when projection of the lifted feasible set onto \((x,t)\) equals the original epigraph or hypograph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace each supported nonlinear epigraph or hypograph by an exact affine conic lift whose projection recovers the original relation.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) has a certified finite-dimensional conic graph template.
The atom occurs in a curvature-compatible epigraph or hypograph position.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted formulation and the original nonlinear relation have identical feasible \((x,t)\)-projections.

notation.meaning: closed convex cone used by the graph template

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: epigraph and hypograph cone lifts are standard conic canonicalization representations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind and exact-lift interpretation fit the leaf, but the precise epigraph/hypograph template and projection-equivalence claim have no cited source.

knowledge_statements.title: Set-Membership Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decomposition of structured convex-set membership into primitive affine cone memberships.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a supported convex set admits the representation \[C=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exists z\in\mathbb{R}^q,\ A_i x+B_i z+b_i\in K_i\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,m\}.\] Canonicalization replaces \(x\in C\) by the displayed primitive memberships and introduces the shared auxiliary variable \(z\). The decomposition is exact precisely when projection of the lifted set onto the \(x\)-coordinates equals \(C\). Equality constraints may be encoded using the zero cone, while multiple memberships may be combined in the product cone \(K_1\times\cdots\times K_m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Express structured set membership as finitely many affine primitive-cone memberships, possibly with auxiliaries, while preserving the projected feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) has a certified finite-dimensional conic representation.
Each \(K_i\) is supported by the canonicalization target.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in C\) holds exactly when an auxiliary \(z\) satisfies every generated primitive membership.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: projection-based decomposition is the standard semantics of conic set lifts
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation matches set-membership decomposition, but no source supports the finite conic lift, zero-cone convention, and exact projection claim as stated.

knowledge_statements.title: Graph Expansion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bottom-up replacement of expression nodes by affine conic graph templates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a normalized expression DAG \(E\) and a library of certified graph templates. Initialize an empty memo table and process nodes in topological order. For each leaf, record its affine representation. For each nonleaf node \(v\), retrieve the representations of its children, instantiate the template for the atom at \(v\), create its fresh auxiliaries and conic constraints, and memoize the affine output representing \(v\). Shared DAG nodes are expanded once. Stop after the root is processed; output the root affine expression, all generated variables, and all generated constraints. Template projection invariants imply equivalence with \(E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Traverse the normalized DAG bottom-up, instantiate each atom’s graph template once, and return an affine root plus generated conic constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is finite, acyclic, normalized, and accepted by the composition rules.
Every nonaffine atom in \(E\) has a certified target-cone template.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Projection of the expanded formulation onto the original variables reproduces the relation represented by \(E\).

notation.meaning: a node of the expression DAG

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: topological template expansion is standard for expression-DAG canonicalization
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits graph expansion, but its traversal, memoization, template-instantiation, and global projection-equivalence guarantees lack inspectable evidence.

children.title: Auxiliary-Variable Generation
children.top_down_role: Creation, naming, shaping, and provenance tracking of canonicalization variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-Variable Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fresh, dimensioned variable creation during template instantiation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each instantiated template occurrence \(o\), read its ordered auxiliary blocks with dimensions \(d_{o,1},\ldots,d_{o,r_o}\). Initialize the unused-index counter at the next available coordinate. Allocate disjoint variables \(z_{o,j}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{o,j}}\), advance the counter by \(d_{o,j}\), and bind each template placeholder to its allocated block. Reuse a block only when the template explicitly declares sharing for the same memoized DAG occurrence. Stop after all placeholders are bound; output the extended variable vector and the occurrence-to-coordinate map. Freshness prevents unintended equality couplings between independent template occurrences.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocate correctly dimensioned, disjoint auxiliary blocks for template placeholders and record their coordinates, reusing them only for explicitly shared occurrences.
assumptions_latex: Each template declares the dimensions and sharing policy of its auxiliary blocks.
The current variable-coordinate range is known.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every placeholder has a unique well-typed binding, except for sharing explicitly required by the template.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: freshness and dimensional consistency are standard variable-generation invariants
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Constraint Generation
children.top_down_role: Creation and classification of affine, set-membership, or cone constraints during graph expansion.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instantiation and assembly of primitive conic constraints from graph templates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each template occurrence \(o\), substitute its canonical affine child representations and allocated auxiliary blocks into every declared relation. Convert each relation to \(F_{o,k}w+g_{o,k}\in K_{o,k}\), where \(w\) is the assembled variable vector. Check dimensions, preserve the cone-block order, and append the relation to the global constraint list. Equalities use an explicit zero-cone block. Stop after all occurrences are instantiated; output either the ordered block system or the product-cone form \[Fw+g\in K,\qquad K=\prod_{o,k}K_{o,k}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Substitute affine children and auxiliaries into each template, validate dimensions, and assemble the resulting primitive memberships into one conic system.
assumptions_latex: All template placeholders have well-typed affine or auxiliary bindings.
Every declared cone block is supported by the target representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generated constraints form the product-cone system \(Fw+g\in K\) prescribed by the instantiated templates.

notation.meaning: assembled original and auxiliary variable vector
cone block for one generated relation

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: affine cone-block assembly is standard in conic canonicalization

children.title: Generation Provenance Metadata
children.top_down_role: Mappings from generated variables or constraints to originating symbolic expressions.

knowledge_statements.title: Generation Provenance Metadata
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metadata linking generated conic objects to source expressions and transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Generation provenance metadata for a canonicalized instance is a finite map \(\Pi\) assigning each generated variable block or constraint block \(g\) a tuple \[\Pi(g)=(s,o,r,p),\] where \(s\) identifies the originating source-expression node or source constraint, \(o\) identifies the template occurrence, \(r\) names the transformation rule, and \(p\) records the coordinate or cone-block placement. The map is complete when every generated object has an entry, and traceable when repeatedly following source identifiers terminates at an original model object. Metadata is observational and does not alter the generated feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Provenance maps every generated variable or constraint block to its source object, template occurrence, transformation rule, and final placement.
assumptions_latex: Generated objects and source model objects have stable identifiers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Completeness and traceability of \(\Pi\) permit every generated block to be attributed to an original model object.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: source-to-generated-object maps are standard canonicalization provenance structures
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the provenance-metadata leaf, but this particular tuple schema and its completeness and traceability criteria are system-design choices requiring a source.

children.title: Canonicalization Growth Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Model-size expansion, duplication, and structural overhead caused by generated objects.

knowledge_statements.title: Canonicalization Growth Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Output-size bound for local, bounded-arity template expansion of an expression DAG.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a normalized expression DAG contain \(N\) distinct expanded nodes. If the template selected at node \(v\) creates at most \(a_v\) scalar auxiliary coordinates, \(c_v\) primitive constraint blocks, and \(s_v\) scalar affine coefficients, then memoized graph expansion creates at most \[A=\sum_v a_v,\qquad C=\sum_v c_v,\qquad S=\sum_v s_v\] such objects. Consequently, if \(a_v\le\bar a\), \(c_v\le\bar c\), and \(s_v\le\bar s\) uniformly, output size and construction work are \(O(N(\bar a+\bar c+\bar s))\) in a unit-cost sparse-assembly model. Exponential growth remains possible when template sizes themselves grow exponentially with encoded atom parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonicalization grows linearly in distinct DAG nodes when local template sizes are uniformly bounded; parameter-dependent templates can violate this boundary.
assumptions_latex: Shared DAG nodes are memoized and expanded once.
Sparse coefficient insertion and index creation have unit cost.
Template output sizes \(a_v,c_v,s_v\) are explicitly available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generated size is bounded by \(A+C+S\), yielding the stated linear bound under uniform local limits.

notation.meaning: number of distinct expanded DAG nodes
total auxiliary coordinates, constraint blocks, and affine coefficients

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: additive output bounds follow from memoized local-template expansion
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the leaf, but the sparse unit-cost model, additive size accounting, construction-work bound, and exponential-growth boundary require a formal source.

knowledge_statements.title: Problem-Class Analysis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static classification of a validated model before selection of a reduction chain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a validated optimization model \(P\). Traverse its objective, constraints, variables, parameters, and attributes; compute required structural features, including curvature class, integrality, quadratic structure, cone families, complex or matrix domains, and parameter dependence. Initialize the most specific recognized class and widen it whenever an encountered feature is unsupported by that class. Reject if a required semantic attribute is inconsistent or unknown. Stop after all objects are visited; output a descriptor \(D(P)\) containing the recognized problem class and the complete set \(R(P)\) of representation capabilities required by any semantics-preserving reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inspect all model objects to classify the problem and enumerate every capability a valid reduction chain must preserve or implement.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is finite and its expression attributes have been validated.
The analyzer has a declared hierarchy of problem classes and feature rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D(P)\) classifies \(P\), and \(R(P)\) contains every detected capability required for its reduction.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: feature-based static classification is standard in reduction-chain selection
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits problem-class analysis, but the feature hierarchy, widening procedure, rejection rule, and claimed completeness of the capability set are architecture-specific and uncited.

knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Capability Matching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility condition for assigning a canonicalized problem to a solver or reduction chain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R(P)\) be the capabilities required by problem \(P\), let \(T\) be a candidate reduction chain, and let \(C(S)\) be solver \(S\)'s declared capabilities. The pair \((T,S)\) is admissible exactly when \(T\) is semantics preserving on the class of \(P\), every reduction precondition holds, and \[R(T(P))\subseteq C(S).\] Capability comparison includes variable domains, supported cone blocks, integrality, objective direction, coefficient representation, and any requested solution information. If no admissible pair exists, matching must return an explicit unsupported-capability set rather than silently weaken the model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver-chain pair is admissible only when reductions apply without semantic loss and the solver supports every capability required by the reduced problem.
assumptions_latex: Solver capability declarations and reduction preconditions are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Matching succeeds exactly for pairs \((T,S)\) satisfying semantic applicability and \(R(T(P))\subseteq C(S)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: capability inclusion plus reduction applicability is the standard matching predicate
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits solver-capability matching, but capability-set inclusion alone is an architecture-dependent abstraction; the claimed exact admissibility criterion needs an authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.title: Middle-End Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-independent semantic reductions between validated models and primitive conic form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a validated model \(P_0\) and an ordered list of applicable solver-independent reductions \(R_1,\ldots,R_k\). Initialize an empty inverse-data stack. For \(i=1,\ldots,k\), verify the precondition of \(R_i\), compute \((P_i,I_i)=R_i(P_{i-1})\), and push inverse data \(I_i\). Typical steps eliminate complex variables, normalize objectives, convert structured constraints, and expand nonlinear atoms into affine conic graph forms. Stop after the target intermediate class is reached; output \(P_k\) and \((I_1,\ldots,I_k)\). Each step must preserve feasible projections, objective values, and recoverable solution information specified by its contract.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply solver-independent reductions in order, recording inverse data so feasibility, objective values, and requested solutions remain recoverable.
assumptions_latex: Every selected reduction has a checked precondition and a semantic contract.
The chain terminates in the designated intermediate problem class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_k\) is equivalent to \(P_0\) under the composed reduction contracts, with recovery data \((I_1,\ldots,I_k)\).

notation.meaning: inverse or solution-recovery data for that reduction

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: composable reductions with inverse-data stacks are standard modeling-system architecture
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits middle-end reductions, but the selected reduction family, inverse-data protocol, termination target, and preservation guarantees lack inspectable support.

knowledge_statements.title: Back-End Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-specific conversion of an intermediate conic problem into a solver interface instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an intermediate problem \(P\), a selected solver \(S\), and its interface contract. Initialize solver data and an inverse-data stack. Apply solver-specific reductions that reorder cone blocks, split or combine supported cones, translate bounds and equalities, choose matrix vectorizations, and map coefficients into the solver's sparse storage format. After each step, validate dimensions and capability compatibility and record the inverse mapping. Stop when the result matches the native input schema of \(S\); output solver data \(D_S\) and recovery map \(J_S\). Applying \(J_S\) to a returned solution restores the requested coordinates and statuses whenever the solver supplies them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Translate an intermediate conic problem into a chosen solver’s native data layout while recording mappings needed to recover requested results.
assumptions_latex: The selected solver supports every cone and domain remaining in \(P\).
Each back-end transformation has a validated inverse mapping for requested solution fields.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_S\) conforms to the native schema of \(S\), and \(J_S\) maps supported solver results back to the intermediate model.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: solver-specific data conversion with inverse mappings is standard back-end architecture
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits back-end reductions, but the solver-specific transformations and recovery guarantees are architecture and interface claims requiring a cited source with a precise locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Alternative Canonicalization Targets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criteria for interchangeable intermediate conic targets within a reduction chain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an original minimization problem have nonempty feasible set \(F\), objective \(f:F\to\mathbb R\), and nonempty optimizer set \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\). A target \((F_i,g_i)\) is exactly recoverable when there are maps \(E_i:F\to F_i\) and \(R_i:F_i\to F\), together with constants \(a_i>0\) and \(b_i\in\mathbb R\), such that \(R_i(E_i(x))=x\) for every \(x\in F\) and \(g_i(z)=a_i f(R_i(z))+b_i\) for every \(z\in F_i\). If the target optimum is attained, then \(R_i(\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in F_i}g_i(z))=S\). Two such targets are interchangeable with respect to optimal solutions when both satisfy these conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exactly recoverable target maps every target-feasible point back to an original-feasible point, preserves the objective through a positive affine transformation, and recovers exactly the original optimizer set.
assumptions_latex: Each target feasible set is nonempty and its optimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_i(\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in F_i}g_i(z))=S\) for every exactly recoverable target \(i\).

notation.meaning: positive objective scaling and additive offset

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact recovery and positive affine objective transformations are standard invariants of optimization reductions

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix Stuffing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instantiation of a fixed conic-program template from numerical parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a parameter vector \(\theta\), fixed sparsity maps \(I_A,I_b,I_c\), and coefficient functions \(v_A(\theta)\), \(v_b(\theta)\), and \(v_c(\theta)\). Initialize zero arrays with the prescribed solver dimensions; place the returned values at their indexed positions, summing entries whose matrix indices coincide. Preserve the predetermined variable ordering and cone-block ordering. Output numerical data \((A(\theta),b(\theta),c(\theta),K)\) defining \(\min_x c(\theta)^Tx\) subject to \(A(\theta)x+s=b(\theta)\) and \(s\in K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix stuffing evaluates parameter-dependent coefficients and inserts them into a fixed sparse conic template without rebuilding the symbolic reduction.
assumptions_latex: The symbolic structure and all array dimensions are independent of \(\theta\).
Every coefficient function is defined at the supplied \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output arrays instantiate the prescribed conic template at \(\theta\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: matrix stuffing conventionally separates symbolic sparsity analysis from numerical parameter insertion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and content kind fit Matrix Stuffing, but no inspectable modeling-system source supports the fixed-template, duplicate-summation, and ordering conventions.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Coefficient Assembly
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic construction of sparse solver arrays from canonical coefficient contributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input matrix contributions \((i_k,j_k,v_k)\) for \(k=1,\ldots,N\) and declared dimensions \(m,n\). Reject any contribution outside \(1\le i_k\le m\) or \(1\le j_k\le n\). Group contributions by the pair \((i_k,j_k)\), replace each group by its sum, discard a summed value only under the declared numerical-zero policy, and sort the surviving indices in the solver-required order. Output a sparse matrix \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) satisfying \(A_{ij}=\sum_{k:(i_k,j_k)=(i,j)}v_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse assembly validates coefficient addresses, sums duplicates, applies a declared zero policy, and emits entries in the solver’s required order.
assumptions_latex: All values \(v_k\) belong to a common numerical scalar type.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_{ij}=\sum_{k:(i_k,j_k)=(i,j)}v_k\) for every declared matrix position.

notation.meaning: row, column, and value of contribution k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: coordinate sparse assembly sums all contributions sharing an index pair

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sparse assembly algorithm is mathematically coherent and locally appropriate, but its numerical-zero and solver-ordering requirements need an implementation or sparse-format specification.

children.title: Cone-Dimension Metadata
children.top_down_role: Cone-type counts, block dimensions, multiplicities, and product-cone structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Dimension Metadata
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension data describing an ordered product of primitive cone blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an ordered cone product \(K=K_1\times\cdots\times K_q\), cone-dimension metadata is the ordered sequence \(D=((\tau_1,d_1),\ldots,(\tau_q,d_q))\), where \(\tau_j\) identifies the primitive cone family and \(d_j\in\mathbb N_0\) is the number of scalar coordinates occupied by \(K_j\) in the solver vectorization. The metadata are valid only when each \((\tau_j,d_j)\) denotes a supported cone block and the total slack-vector length is \(m=\sum_{j=1}^q d_j\). Structured cones must use the solver’s declared vectorized dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cone-dimension metadata records each ordered cone type and its scalar storage dimension, whose sum equals the slack-vector length.
assumptions_latex: The solver supplies an unambiguous vectorization convention for every structured cone family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\) determines the ordered block types and total scalar dimension \(m\).

notation.meaning: scalar storage dimension of block j

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: product-cone data require ordered block types and scalar dimensions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but supported cone descriptors and structured-cone vectorized dimensions are solver-interface conventions requiring a cited specification.

children.title: Cone-Offset Metadata
children.top_down_role: Starting coordinates, block spans, and segment boundaries in solver vectors.

knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Offset Metadata
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prefix offsets locating cone blocks in a flattened solver vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given ordered block dimensions \(d_1,\ldots,d_q\), cone-offset metadata are integers \(o_1,\ldots,o_{q+1}\) defined by \(o_1=0\) and \(o_{j+1}=o_j+d_j\) for \(j=1,\ldots,q\). Under zero-based half-open indexing, block \(j\) occupies coordinates \([o_j,o_{j+1})\), and \(o_{q+1}=\sum_{j=1}^q d_j\) is the flattened vector length. Thus the block intervals are consecutive and pairwise disjoint, with union \([0,o_{q+1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cone offsets are prefix sums of ordered block dimensions and locate each block as a disjoint half-open slice.

notation.meaning: starting scalar offset of cone block j

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: contiguous block offsets are prefix sums of block dimensions

children.title: Dimension-to-Offset Mappings
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between declared cone dimensions and solver-data coordinate ranges.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-to-Offset Mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mapping ordered cone dimensions to global coordinate addresses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(d=(d_1,\ldots,d_q)\), define \(P(d)_1=0\) and \(P(d)_{j+1}=\sum_{k=1}^{j}d_k\). Let \(L_d=\{(j,r):1\le j\le q,\ r\in\mathbb Z,\ 0\le r<d_j\}\) and \(G_d=\{t\in\mathbb Z:0\le t<\sum_{k=1}^q d_k\}\). Define \(\phi_d:L_d\to G_d\) by \(\phi_d(j,r)=P(d)_j+r\). Every \(t\in G_d\) has a unique index \(j\) satisfying \(P(d)_j\le t<P(d)_{j+1}\), with local coordinate \(r=t-P(d)_j\). Hence \(\phi_d\) is a bijection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prefix sums map every valid block-local coordinate bijectively to a flattened coordinate, including when some blocks have dimension zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi_d:L_d\to G_d\) is bijective.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: prefix sums induce the canonical bijection between block-local and flattened indices

children.title: Metadata Consistency Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Mismatches among cone declarations, offsets, matrix rows, and recovery records.

knowledge_statements.title: Metadata Consistency Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary consistency predicate for coefficient arrays, cone blocks, and address metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Metadata \((D,o,m)\), with \(D=((\tau_j,d_j))_{j=1}^q\), are consistent with solver data \((A,b,c)\) precisely when: \(o_1=0\), \(o_{j+1}-o_j=d_j\), and \(o_{q+1}=m\); every block descriptor \((\tau_j,d_j)\) is supported; \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\); and every stored row or cone-coordinate address lies in its declared half-open interval. Crossing any such dimension, type, or address boundary invalidates the assembled instance before solver invocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metadata are consistent exactly when offsets, dimensions, cone types, array shapes, and all stored addresses agree.
assumptions_latex: A solver-specific table defines supported block descriptors and their scalar dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The assembled instance is admissible only if all stated equalities, support tests, shapes, and address bounds hold.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: array and cone metadata must share dimensions and valid address ranges

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but “precisely when” depends on a solver-specific support table and may omit other solver validity requirements. A validation specification is needed before accepting the biconditional.

knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Specific Standard Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adapter representation between a generic conic form and a solver’s accepted convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax+s=b\) and \(s\in K\). A solver-specific standard-form adapter consists of invertible variable and residual maps \(x=T_xz\) and \(r=T_r(A T_xz-b)\), together with the transformed cone \(K_s=T_rK\), objective data \(c_s=T_x^Tc\), and any required permutations or vectorizations encoded in \(T_x,T_r\). The emitted equalities, inequalities, and cone blocks must be algebraically equivalent to \(T_r(AT_xz+s-b)=0\). Recovery applies \(T_x\) and \(T_r^{-1}\), so feasibility and objective values are preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver adapter applies declared invertible coordinate, sign, permutation, and vectorization maps while preserving the generic conic problem.
assumptions_latex: \(T_x\) and \(T_r\) are invertible on their represented spaces.
The solver supports the transformed cone \(K_s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Solver-form feasibility is equivalent to \(Ax+s=b\), \(s\in K\), and \(c_s^Tz=c^Tx\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Loss of Injectivity Prevents Unique Primal Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifiability boundary for deterministic inverse recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let E:X\to Z be the complete retained forward map from original to canonical primal coordinates. A recovery map R satisfying R(E(x))=x for every x\in X exists only if E is injective on X. If E(x_1)=E(x_2) for distinct x_1,x_2, the canonical point alone cannot determine both originals; recovery can return only an equivalence class or a representative selected using additional stored data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unique primal recovery is impossible when two distinct original points have the same complete retained canonical image.
assumptions_latex: E\text{ contains all information retained for primal recovery}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\exists R\;\forall x\in X,\ R(E(x))=x)\Rightarrow E\text{ is injective on }X.
knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Injectivity Prevents Unique Primal Recovery
Primal-Variable Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse application of reduction records to recover original primal variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a solver primal solution \(z_L\) and an ordered reduction chain with recorded inverse maps \(R_L,\ldots,R_1\). For \(k=L,L-1,\ldots,1\), compute \(z_{k-1}=R_k(z_k)\), undoing recorded permutations, scalings, affine substitutions, and projections while discarding auxiliary variables only after their defining relations have been evaluated. Output the components of \(z_0\) corresponding to the original variable blocks. Recovery is valid when each inverse record satisfies \(R_k(E_k(u))=u\) on the feasible domain of its forward reduction \(E_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal recovery reverses reduction records in last-in-first-out order and extracts the original variable blocks after undoing transformations.
assumptions_latex: Every forward reduction stores a dimensionally compatible inverse record.
The solver solution lies in the domain of each successive inverse map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every feasible original point \(x\), recovery from \(E_L\circ\cdots\circ E_1(x)\) returns \(x\).

notation.meaning: forward and inverse maps for reduction stage k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: composed reductions are inverted in reverse order using stored transformation data

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reverse-order recovery algorithm fits the leaf, but the rules for projections, auxiliary-variable removal, and stored inverse records require a canonicalization-system source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Only the Adjoint Aggregate Is Canonically Recoverable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifiability boundary under constraint aggregation or elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If canonical residuals satisfy r_c=Mr_o, a canonical multiplier y_c induces the original-residual functional y_o=M^{\mathsf T}y_c through \langle y_c,r_c\rangle=\langle M^{\mathsf T}y_c,r_o\rangle. This adjoint aggregate is canonical. It does not, without additional stored rules, identify historical multipliers assigned separately to constraints or residual directions discarded by M; moreover, original multipliers outside \operatorname{range}(M^{\mathsf T}) cannot be represented by this pullback.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adjoint pullback recovers the aggregate original-residual functional, not necessarily unique historical multipliers for eliminated constraints.
assumptions_latex: The two residual spaces use the declared compatible inner products.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y_o=M^{\mathsf T}y_c\text{ is the canonical pullback, while eliminated individual multipliers need not be identifiable}.

notation.meaning: map from original to canonical residual coordinates
canonical multiplier and its original-residual pullback

knowledge_statements.title: Only the Adjoint Aggregate Is Canonically Recoverable
Dual-Variable Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adjoint recovery of multipliers through affine canonicalization stages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input solver multipliers \(y_L\) and reduction records. Traverse the records in reverse order. If stage \(k\) represents an original residual \(r_{k-1}\) as \(r_k=M_kr_{k-1}\), set \(y_{k-1}=M_k^Ty_k\), because \(y_k^Tr_k=(M_k^Ty_k)^Tr_{k-1}\). Undo recorded cone-block permutations and dual scalings, aggregate multipliers of split constraints, and remove multipliers belonging solely to introduced defining constraints. Output multipliers indexed by the original constraints. The output is valid only when every eliminated or aggregated multiplier has a recorded adjoint rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual recovery reverses residual transformations by adjoints, undoes block conventions, aggregates split constraints, and returns original-constraint multipliers.
assumptions_latex: Each reduction records its residual map and multiplier aggregation rule.
All multiplier and residual pairings use compatible inner products.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recovered multiplier preserves the pairing \(y_L^Tr_L=y_0^Tr_0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimizer Preservation Does Not Imply Affine Value Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of scale-and-offset objective reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Equality of minimizing decisions does not imply an affine relation between objective values. Minimizing \|Ax-b\|_2^2 and minimizing \|Ax-b\|_2 has the same minimizers, but the reported values satisfy v_{\rm sq}=v_{\rm norm}^2 rather than a uniform affine relation. Objective recovery must therefore store the actual value transformation; affine scale-offset inversion applies only when that recorded transformation is affine and injective on the relevant range.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reformulation can preserve minimizers while changing objective values nonaffinely, as least squares and residual-norm minimization demonstrate.
assumptions_latex: The residual norm is nonnegative and the square function is increasing on its range.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}f=\operatorname*{argmin}g\not\Rightarrow f=\alpha g+\beta.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimizer Preservation Does Not Imply Affine Value Preservation
Objective-Value Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of the original objective from solver-reported values and stored transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose canonicalization records the solver objective as \(g(z)=\alpha f(R(z))+\beta\), where \(f\) is the original objective, \(R\) is primal recovery, \(\alpha>0\), and \(\beta\in\mathbb R\). For a solver point \(z\) with reported value \(v_s=g(z)\), reconstruct \(v_o=(v_s-\beta)/\alpha\). If the solver does not report a reliable value, compute \(v_o=f(R(z))\) directly. Agreement requires \(|v_s-(\alpha f(R(z))+\beta)|\le\varepsilon_{m obj}\) under the declared numerical tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The original objective is recovered by undoing stored positive scaling and offset, then checked against direct evaluation at recovered variables.
assumptions_latex: The recovery map and original objective are defined at the returned point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_o=f(R(z))=(v_s-\beta)/\alpha\) in exact arithmetic.

notation.meaning: solver and reconstructed original objective values

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: affine objective transformations are inverted algebraically and checked by direct evaluation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine objective reconstruction is algebraically precise and the representation kind is defensible, but the solver-value reliability fallback and consistency tolerance require an interface reference.

children.title: Residual Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of original constraint residuals from canonical solver outputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Original-space optimality residuals computed after primal and dual recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the recovered conic problem \(\min_x c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax+s=b\), \(s\in K\), with recovered multiplier \(y\in K^*\), reconstruct the primal residual \(r_p=Ax+s-b\), dual residual \(r_d=A^Ty+c\), complementarity residual \(r_c=\langle s,y\rangle\), and gap \(r_g=c^Tx+b^Ty\). A scale-aware report may use \(\|r_p\|/(1+\|b\|)\), \(\|r_d\|/(1+\|c\|)\), and \(|r_g|/(1+|c^Tx|+|b^Ty|)\). These quantities must be evaluated in original coordinates, not copied from transformed solver residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual reconstruction recomputes primal feasibility, dual feasibility, complementarity, and gap in original coordinates with declared scaling.
assumptions_latex: The multiplier convention is \(y\in K^*\) with dual objective \(-b^Ty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact primal-dual optimality implies \(r_p=0\), \(r_d=0\), \(r_c=0\), and \(r_g=0\).

notation.meaning: original-space primal and dual feasibility residuals

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual components not represented by affine stationarity and gap diagnostics alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For recovered (x,s,y) under Ax+s=b, s\in K, and y\in K^*, define r_K=\operatorname{dist}(s,K) and r_{K^*}=\operatorname{dist}(y,K^*). For each recorded bridge equation B_j(x,u_j)=0, define r_{B,j}=B_j(x,u_j); cone-valued bridge conditions are tested by distance to their declared cones. Exact recovered feasibility requires these residuals to vanish in addition to the applicable affine residuals. Small affine residuals alone do not certify cone membership or bridge consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual reconstruction includes primal and dual cone distances and every recorded bridge residual, not only affine equations.
assumptions_latex: Distances and residual norms are declared.
Every bridge relation needed to interpret auxiliary variables is recorded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_K=r_{K^*}=0\text{ and all bridge residuals vanish for exact recovered cone and bridge feasibility}.

notation.meaning: distance from u to set C in the declared norm

knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Membership and Bridge Residuals

children.title: Reconstruction Consistency Checks
children.top_down_role: Consistency boundaries linking reconstructed quantities to the source model.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic validation limited to canonical coordinates determined by the recovered original point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let E be the recorded forward canonicalization, R the recovery map, and \pi select canonical coordinates uniquely determined by the original variables. For a returned canonical point z, the identity \pi(E(R(z)))=\pi(z) certifies consistency on those coordinates. Introduced auxiliary coordinates must separately satisfy their recorded defining equations or cone relations; they need not equal a newly generated auxiliary choice when the representation is nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forwarding a recovered point must reproduce every uniquely determined canonical coordinate, while nonunique auxiliaries are checked by their defining relations.
assumptions_latex: \pi\text{ excludes canonical coordinates not uniquely determined by the recovered original point}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \pi(E(R(z)))=\pi(z),\quad\text{with all recorded auxiliary defining relations satisfied}.

notation.meaning: projection onto canonical coordinates uniquely determined by original variables

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Forward-Recovery Consistency

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tolerance Checks Are Not Exact Certificates Without Error Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary on floating-point reconstruction checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Passing residual comparisons with a positive tolerance \varepsilon certifies only the stated approximate inequalities. It does not imply exact feasibility, exact objective equality, or exact bridge satisfaction unless independent error bounds justify that conclusion. Conversely, failure at one tolerance rejects that numerical reconstruction but does not prove that no valid original solution exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-tolerance consistency is an approximate diagnostic, not an exact certificate without additional error analysis.
assumptions_latex: Acceptance uses nonzero-tolerance inequalities or finite-precision evaluations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{residual}\le\varepsilon\not\Rightarrow\operatorname{residual}=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance Checks Are Not Exact Certificates Without Error Bounds
Reconstruction Consistency Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checks recovered primal variables, objective values, and residuals against the original model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original problem be \(\min_x f_0(x)\) subject to \(f_i(x)\le 0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\) and \(h(x)=0\). Given recovered \(\widehat x\), reconstructed objective \(\widehat v\), reported residual vector \(\widehat r\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge 0\), reconstruction is consistent when \[|\widehat v-f_0(\widehat x)|\le\varepsilon,\qquad \max_i(f_i(\widehat x))_+\le\varepsilon,\qquad \|h(\widehat x)\|\le\varepsilon,\] and each component of \(\widehat r\) agrees within \(\varepsilon\) with the corresponding residual recomputed from \(\widehat x\). Failure of any comparison invalidates the recovered result at tolerance \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recovery is consistent only when reconstructed objectives and residuals agree with values recomputed in the original model within the chosen tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(f_0,f_i\) and \(h\) are evaluable at the recovered point.
The residual components have fixed meanings shared by reconstruction and direct evaluation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All reconstructed quantities agree with direct original-model evaluation to tolerance \(\varepsilon\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf and is mathematically coherent, but no cited source supports this particular reconstruction protocol, residual correspondence, or invalidation rule.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Infeasibility Alone Does Not Establish Primal Unboundedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary for translating paired conic statuses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a conic primal-dual pair, primal unboundedness implies dual infeasibility, but dual infeasibility alone does not generally imply primal unboundedness because the primal can also be infeasible. Translating backend dual infeasibility to original-model unboundedness therefore requires a recovered primal feasible base point and an improving recession direction, or another theorem whose stated assumptions yield unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual infeasibility cannot automatically be translated to primal unboundedness because both paired problems may be infeasible.
assumptions_latex: Statuses refer to a consistently oriented primal-dual conic pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{dual infeasible}\not\Rightarrow\text{primal unbounded}.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Infeasibility Alone Does Not Establish Primal Unboundedness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rule for translating exact, approximate, interrupted, and indeterminate outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After fixing backend-specific status meanings and target certificate predicates, translation may preserve or weaken a backend conclusion when inverse validation loses evidence, but it may not strengthen it. In particular, an inaccurate, interrupted, or certificate-free result cannot become an exact optimal, infeasible, or unbounded original-model status solely by relabeling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Status translation may weaken a conclusion after failed recovery, but cannot strengthen unsupported evidence.
assumptions_latex: Backend status semantics are explicitly declared.
Each conclusive target status has a declared validation predicate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{strength}(\tau(s,d))\le \operatorname{strength}(s,d)\text{ under the declared evidence preorder}.
knowledge_statements.title: Evidence-Monotone Status Translation
Solver-Status Translation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maps backend termination statuses to original-problem statuses while preserving uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be the backend status set, \(T\) the modeling-system status set, and \(\tau:S\times D\to T\) a translation using diagnostic data \(D\). A valid translation satisfies \[\tau(\mathrm{optimal},d)=\mathrm{optimal},\quad \tau(\mathrm{primal\ infeasible},d)=\mathrm{infeasible},\quad \tau(\mathrm{dual\ infeasible},d)=\mathrm{unbounded}\] only when the canonicalization preserves feasibility and primal-dual interpretation and the corresponding certificate passes inverse-recovery checks. Ambiguous, inaccurate, interrupted, or certificate-free backend outcomes must map to an uncertainty-preserving status rather than a stronger conclusion. Backend status, diagnostic accuracy, and certificate availability remain separately recoverable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Translate solver statuses only when canonicalization and certificates justify the interpretation; otherwise retain an uncertain or interrupted status.
assumptions_latex: Canonicalization preserves the original problem's feasibility and objective interpretation.
Required infeasibility or unboundedness certificates can be mapped back to the original model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The translated status is no stronger than the conclusion supported by backend diagnostics and recovered certificates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the leaf, but status meanings and the translation from dual infeasibility to original-model unboundedness depend on solver conventions, certificates, and canonicalization details for which no source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameterized Problem Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines when parameters change numerical data without changing canonical conic structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A family indexed by \(\theta\in\Theta\) has fixed parameterized conic structure if every instance canonicalizes as \[\min_z\ c(\theta)^Tz+d(\theta)\quad\text{subject to}\quad A(\theta)z+b(\theta)\in K,\] where the dimension and ordering of \(z\), the row and column sparsity patterns, the product-cone decomposition of \(K\), and the inverse-recovery map are independent of \(\theta\). Parameter dependence may alter stored numerical coefficients but may not alter expression-tree topology, introduce variables or constraints, change cone types or dimensions, or change recovery metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parameterized family has fixed structure when parameter values change coefficients but not dimensions, sparsity layout, cones, or recovery maps.
assumptions_latex: Every instance is accepted by the same canonicalization rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All \(\theta\in\Theta\) share one canonical symbolic structure and differ only through numerical data.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but its strong requirements on sparsity, expression topology, and inverse-recovery metadata are implementation-specific and unsupported by a citation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a fixed-dimension, fixed-sparsity continuously parameterized family, the family–instance distinction, and an illustrative QP parameterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A continuously parameterized optimization problem family has the form \(\operatorname{minimize}_{x\in\mathbb R^n} F_0(x,a)\) subject to \(F_i(x,a)\leq 0\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), and \(H_j(x,a)=0\), \(j=1,\ldots,p\), where \(a\in\mathcal A\subset\mathbb R^\ell\). The functions \(F_0,\ldots,F_m,H_1,\ldots,H_p\) and the parameter set \(\mathcal A\) specify the family; fixing \(a\) specifies one instance. In the stated QP family, \(A,b\) are fixed and \(a=(P,q,G,h)\), with \(P\in\mathbb S_+^n\). For unstructured data, \(\ell=n(n+1)/2+n+mn+m\); if \(P\) is tridiagonal and \(G\) has \(N\) potentially nonzero entries, \(\ell=(2n-1)+n+N+m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuously parameterized problem family is specified by its objective and constraint functions and a finite-dimensional parameter set. Fixing the parameter vector produces one instance. In the chapter's treatment, dimensions and sparsity patterns remain fixed across the family. The QP example varies the positive-semidefinite quadratic matrix, linear term, inequality matrix, and inequality bounds while keeping the equality data fixed.
assumptions_latex: n,m,p\text{ and the prescribed data sparsity patterns are fixed throughout the family}
P\in\mathbb S_+^n\text{ in the QP example, while }A\text{ and }b\text{ are fixed}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Fixing }a\in\mathcal A\text{ yields one problem instance of the specified family.}

knowledge_statements.title: Canonical-Form Caching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Caches symbolic canonicalization when parameter changes preserve conic structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a parameterized model \(P(\theta)\) with fixed canonical structure. At an initial value \(\theta_0\), canonicalize once and store a template \(\mathcal T\) containing dimensions, sparsity locations, cone blocks, coefficient-update maps, and inverse-recovery metadata. For each new \(\theta_k\), verify the structural signature, evaluate only the numerical maps \[\theta_k\longmapsto\bigl(A(\theta_k),b(\theta_k),c(\theta_k),d(\theta_k)\bigr),\] populate the stored locations, and solve the resulting conic instance. If signature validation fails, discard the cache entry and recanonicalize. Stop according to the backend rule and recover the original-model result using the stored metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonicalize once, cache symbolic structure and recovery metadata, then update coefficients for each parameter value unless structural validation fails.
assumptions_latex: The parameterized family has fixed canonical structure.
Coefficient-update maps are evaluable for every admitted parameter value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each structurally compatible instance is produced without repeating symbolic canonicalization.

knowledge_statements.title: Repeated-Solve Data Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Updates cached numerical conic data for successive parameter values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a validated canonical template \(\mathcal T\), update maps \(U_A,U_b,U_c,U_d\), and parameter sequence \((\theta_k)\), initialize the numerical buffers from \(\theta_0\). At iteration \(k\), compute \[A_k=U_A(\theta_k),\qquad b_k=U_b(\theta_k),\qquad c_k=U_c(\theta_k),\qquad d_k=U_d(\theta_k),\] overwrite only the template's designated coefficient locations, optionally supply a dimensionally compatible warm start, and solve the fixed-cone instance. Return the recovered solution and diagnostics. Before every solve, reject the update if a dimension, sparsity pattern, cone block, sign convention, or parameter-domain check differs from \(\mathcal T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each parameter value, update designated coefficient buffers, validate structure, solve the fixed conic form, and recover the original solution.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal T\) is a valid cached canonical template.
Each update map preserves the template's declared array dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A validated update yields the canonical data for the requested parameter instance.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf and is internally consistent, but its validation requirements and update semantics are implementation-specific and have no supporting citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Structure Violations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies parameter changes that invalidate a cached canonical template.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\sigma(P(\theta))\) record the canonical variable dimensions, constraint dimensions, sparsity patterns, cone sequence, expression topology, and recovery metadata of an instance. A parameter-structure violation occurs at \(\theta_1\) relative to cached value \(\theta_0\) when \[\sigma(P(\theta_1))\ne\sigma(P(\theta_0)).\] Typical mechanisms include parameter-controlled dimensions, parameter-dependent indexing, activation or removal of constraints, cone-type changes, and values crossing domains required by atoms. After such a violation, coefficient-only updating is not valid; the system must reject the cached update or perform full canonicalization and construct new recovery metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cached form is invalid when a parameter changes dimensions, topology, sparsity, cones, indexing, atom domains, or recovery metadata.
assumptions_latex: A structural signature is computed independently of numerical coefficient values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\sigma(P(\theta_1))\ne\sigma(P(\theta_0))\), coefficient-only cache reuse is invalid.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but the proposed structural signature and the listed invalidation mechanisms require an authoritative parametric-canonicalization source.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex but Unrecognized Expressions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates mathematical convexity from recognition by a finite composition grammar.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal G\) be a sound but incomplete disciplined-convex grammar. An expression \(e:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is convex but unrecognized when \[e(tx+(1-t)y)\le t e(x)+(1-t)e(y)\] for all \(x,y\in\operatorname{dom}e\) and \(t\in[0,1]\), yet the syntax tree of \(e\) admits no curvature certificate under \(\mathcal G\). Rejection by \(\mathcal G\) therefore establishes only absence of a recognized compositional certificate, not nonconvexity. Canonicalization may proceed only after a compliant equivalent reformulation or extension of the recognized atom rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex expression may be rejected because its syntax lacks a certificate in the modeling grammar; rejection alone does not prove nonconvexity.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal G\) is sound: every expression it certifies as convex is mathematically convex.
\(e\) is convex on its effective domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of \(\mathcal G\) to certify \(e\) does not imply that \(e\) is nonconvex.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure boundary correctly distinguishes convexity from grammar recognition, but no disciplined-convex-programming source is cited for the recognition and rejection claims.

knowledge_statements.title: Equivalent Compliant Rewrites
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reexpresses an unrecognized convex term using supported atoms without changing its modeled value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e(x)\) be an expression and let \(\widetilde e(x,u)\) be built from recognized atoms and constraints, with auxiliary variable \(u\). The rewrite is epigraphically equivalent and compliant when, for every \(x\), \[\operatorname{cl}\{t:t\ge e(x)\}=\operatorname{cl}\{t:\exists u\ \text{such that}\ t\ge\widetilde e(x,u)\ \text{and}\ C(x,u)\},\] and the right-hand system satisfies the recognition grammar and has supported cone representations. Replacing \(t\ge e(x)\) by the right-hand system preserves the closed epigraph and hence preserves minimization values and attainable minimizers whenever closure introduces no unattained boundary optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compliant rewrite uses supported atoms and auxiliaries to reproduce the original closed epigraph, thereby preserving the modeled minimization problem.
assumptions_latex: The auxiliary formulation is accepted by the recognition grammar.
Closure does not create an unattained boundary optimum relevant to the model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original and rewritten epigraph constraints define equivalent minimization models after eliminating \(u\).

notation.meaning: auxiliary variables introduced by the rewrite

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the leaf, but the closure-based epigraph equivalence and its stated consequences for values and minimizers require a source supporting the exact hypotheses.

children.title: Unsupported Atom Targets
children.top_down_role: Recognition failures caused by unavailable atom implementations.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsupported Atom Targets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers recognized atoms lacking a registered canonicalization for the selected backend target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a\) be an atom appearing in a grammar-certified expression, and let \(R(a)\) denote its required graph or epigraph representation. For a target backend with registered atom reductions \(\mathcal A_T\), the atom target is unsupported when \[a\notin\mathcal A_T\] or when no registered reduction expresses \(R(a)\) using the backend's available cones and affine operations. Curvature recognition of \(a\) does not remove this implementation boundary. Canonicalization must fail explicitly unless an equivalent supported rewrite or an alternative backend is selected; silently replacing \(a\) by an inexact representation changes the model unless approximation was requested.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An atom is unsupported when no registered reduction represents it with the selected backend's affine operations and cones, even if its curvature is recognized.
assumptions_latex: The expression containing \(a\) has passed curvature recognition.
The selected backend exposes a fixed set of supported reductions and cones.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(a\notin\mathcal A_T\) and no equivalent supported rewrite exists, exact canonicalization to target \(T\) fails.

notation.meaning: graph or epigraph representation required for the atom

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but registered atom reductions and target-specific failure behavior are implementation-dependent and unsupported by a citation.

children.title: Unsupported Cone Targets
children.top_down_role: Canonical targets outside the available cone library.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsupported Cone Targets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies canonical cone blocks unavailable in the selected solver interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose canonicalization produces \(Az+b\in K\), where \(K=K_1\times\cdots\times K_q\), and let \(\mathcal K_T\) be the cone families accepted by target \(T\). The target is unsupported if some block satisfies \[K_j\notin\mathcal K_T\] and no exact registered lift converts membership in \(K_j\) into affine constraints over cones in \(\mathcal K_T\). The interface must then reject the target or select another exact reduction or solver. Substituting an outer or inner approximation is not an exact target translation and requires a separately declared approximation policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver target is unsupported when a required cone block has neither native support nor an exact registered lift into supported cones.
assumptions_latex: The canonical cone product and its block dimensions are fixed.
Only exact registered lifts count as exact canonicalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If a required \(K_j\) lacks native support and an exact lift, exact translation to target \(T\) fails.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure boundary is coherent and fits the leaf, but native cone support, exact registered lifts, and target rejection behavior require solver-interface evidence.

children.title: Atom-to-Cone Compatibility Failures
children.top_down_role: Mismatches between recognized atoms, graph implementations, and solver cone support.

knowledge_statements.title: Atom-to-Cone Compatibility Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers mismatches between an atom reduction and the dimensions or conventions of available cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a registered reduction for atom \(a\) require cone blocks \(K(a,\delta,s)\), determined by dimension data \(\delta\) and sign or scaling conventions \(s\). Compatibility fails for target \(T\) when the atom is recognized and the nominal cone family is available, but \[K(a,\delta,s)\notin\mathcal K_T(\delta_T,s_T)\] because supported dimensions, vectorization order, symmetry encoding, dual orientation, sign convention, or scaling convention differs. The reduction must not be emitted until an exact adapter reconciles these conventions; otherwise primal feasibility, dual interpretation, or inverse recovery may be incorrect.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatibility fails when atom and solver nominally share a cone family but disagree on dimensions, ordering, orientation, signs, scaling, or encoding.
assumptions_latex: Atom \(a\) has a registered conic reduction.
Target \(T\) nominally supports every required cone family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without an exact convention adapter, the atom reduction is invalid for target \(T\).

notation.meaning: dimension and shape data required by the atom reduction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but the compatibility relation and consequences of encoding, orientation, sign, and scaling mismatches are target-specific and uncited.

children.title: Nonconvex Model Rejection
children.top_down_role: Rejection boundaries for models recognized as nonconvex.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Model Rejection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejects models whose certified curvature contradicts the required convex optimization form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimization of \(f_0(x)\) subject to \(f_i(x)\le0\) and \(h_j(x)=0\). Under a convex-model grammar, the model is admissible only if \(f_0\) and every \(f_i\) are certified convex and every \(h_j\) is certified affine. If any objective or inequality is certified nonconvex, or any equality is certified nonaffine, the convex canonicalization pipeline must reject the model. This rejection concerns the declared formulation; it does not assert that no equivalent convex reformulation exists. Proceeding requires an explicitly selected nonconvex method or a separately validated equivalent compliant rewrite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex pipeline rejects a nonconvex objective or inequality, or a nonaffine equality, while allowing a separately validated convex reformulation.
assumptions_latex: The pipeline targets convex conic optimization.
Curvature and affinity certificates are sound for the recognized grammar.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A certified violation of the convex-form rules prevents convex conic canonicalization of the declared model.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role matches the leaf and the convex-form conditions are standard, but no authoritative disciplined-convex-modeling source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Indeterminate-Curvature Rejection
children.top_down_role: Rejection boundaries for expressions lacking certifiable curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Indeterminate-Curvature Rejection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for sound disciplined-convex canonicalization when an expression’s curvature cannot be certified compositionally.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a sound curvature analyzer assign each expression one of the labels \(\{\mathrm{convex},\mathrm{concave},\mathrm{affine},\mathrm{constant},\mathrm{unknown}\}\). If any objective or constraint needed for a convex model receives \(\mathrm{unknown}\), the disciplined canonicalizer must reject the model rather than emit a conic reformulation. This rejection asserts only failure of the recognition rules: it does not imply that the represented function or feasible set is nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unknown curvature prevents sound conic canonicalization, but rejection certifies only that the rules cannot recognize convexity, not that the model is nonconvex.
assumptions_latex: \(\text{The analyzer’s accepted composition rules are sound for convexity.}\)
\(\text{Canonicalization is permitted only for expressions whose required curvature is certified.}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{unknown}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{reject},\qquad \mathrm{reject}\not\Longrightarrow\mathrm{nonconvex}.\)

notation.meaning: curvature not certified by the recognition system

review_flags: Exact disciplined-convex recognition specification is not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role and mathematical distinction are appropriate, but the mandatory rejection behavior depends on the disciplined-canonicalization specification and has no cited source.

children.title: Rejection Diagnostic Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Diagnostic distinctions among structural rejection outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Rejection Diagnostic Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic limits on conclusions drawn from canonicalizer rejection diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a sound but incomplete disciplined canonicalizer \(C\), let \(C(M)=\mathrm{accept}\) mean that model \(M\) has been certified and conically reduced. If \(C(M)=\mathrm{reject}(e,r)\), the diagnostic may identify an offending expression \(e\) and failed rule \(r\), but it certifies only that this recognition path failed. It does not certify infeasibility, unboundedness, nonconvexity, or absence of an equivalent conic formulation obtainable after algebraic reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rejection diagnostic locates a failed recognition rule; it does not establish nonconvexity, infeasibility, unboundedness, or impossibility of another conic formulation.
assumptions_latex: \(C\text{ is sound but not assumed complete.}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C(M)=\mathrm{reject}(e,r)\Longrightarrow\text{rule }r\text{ failed at }e\), with no stronger model-level conclusion.
review_flags: Canonicalizer-specific diagnostic semantics require a primary specification.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral-Uncertainty Counterparts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP-dual counterpart of a scalar robust affine inequality over a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R^m:Fu\le g\}\) be nonempty, and suppose \(\sup_{u\in U}q(x)^\top u\) is finite. Then the robust inequality \(a(x)+q(x)^\top u\le0\) for every \(u\in U\) holds if and only if there exists \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfying \(F^\top\lambda=q(x)\) and \(a(x)+g^\top\lambda\le0\). Thus polyhedral uncertainty introduces nonnegative LP-dual variables and affine constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust affine inequality over a nonempty polyhedron becomes affine constraints involving a nonnegative multiplier from linear-programming duality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a(x)+q(x)^\top u\le0\ \forall u\in U\iff\exists\lambda\ge0:\ F^\top\lambda=q(x),\ a(x)+g^\top\lambda\le0.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Norm-Ball Uncertainty Counterparts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-norm counterpart of a scalar robust affine inequality over an affine norm ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\{\bar u+Pz:z\in\mathbb R^k,\ \|z\|_p\le\rho\}\), where \(\rho\ge0\) and \(1\le p\le\infty\). With \(p_*\) defined by \(1/p+1/p_*=1\), the robust inequality \(a(x)+q(x)^\top u\le0\) for every \(u\in U\) is equivalent to \(a(x)+q(x)^\top\bar u+\rho\|P^\top q(x)\|_{p_*}\le0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximizing an affine uncertain term over a norm ball produces the corresponding dual norm, yielding an exact deterministic inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(a(x)\text{ and }q(x)\text{ are finite at the candidate }x.\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a(x)+q(x)^\top u\le0\ \forall u\in U\iff a(x)+q(x)^\top\bar u+\rho\|P^\top q(x)\|_{p_*}\le0.\)

notation.meaning: affine image of a radius-rho norm ball

knowledge_statements.title: Ellipsoidal-Uncertainty SOC Counterparts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order-cone counterpart for affine uncertainty ranging over an ellipsoid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\{\bar u+Pz:z\in\mathbb R^k,\ \|z\|_2\le1\}\). The robust affine inequality \(a(x)+q(x)^\top u\le0\) for every \(u\in U\) is equivalent to \(a(x)+q(x)^\top\bar u+\|P^\top q(x)\|_2\le0\). Equivalently, there exists \(t\ge0\) with \(\|P^\top q(x)\|_2\le t\) and \(a(x)+q(x)^\top\bar u+t\le0\), which is an SOC representation when the displayed mappings are affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine robust inequality over an ellipsoid is exactly represented by one Euclidean-norm bound and one scalar inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(a\text{ and }q\text{ are affine when an SOC model is claimed.}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a(x)+q(x)^\top u\le0\ \forall u\in U\iff\exists t\ge0:\ \|P^\top q(x)\|_2\le t,\ a(x)+q(x)^\top\bar u+t\le0.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Product Uncertainty Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable support function for a Cartesian product of independent uncertainty blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty sets \(U_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{m_i}\), define \(U=U_1\times\cdots\times U_k\). For \(y=(y_1,\ldots,y_k)\), the support function separates as \(\sigma_U(y)=\sum_{i=1}^k\sigma_{U_i}(y_i)\), with equality in the extended-real sense. Consequently, a robust affine term whose uncertainty blocks range independently over \(U_i\) is canonicalized by summing the individual block support-function counterparts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support function of a Cartesian product equals the sum of the component support functions, so independent uncertainty blocks canonicalize separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_U(y_1,\ldots,y_k)=\sum_{i=1}^k\sigma_{U_i}(y_i).\)

notation.meaning: support function sup over u in U of y transpose u

knowledge_statements.title: Intersection Uncertainty Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infimal-convolution representation of the support function of a qualified convex intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_1,\ldots,U_k\) be nonempty closed convex subsets of \(\mathbb R^m\), and suppose \(\bigcap_{i=1}^k\operatorname{ri}U_i\ne\varnothing\). For every \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), the support function of their intersection satisfies \(\sigma_{\cap_iU_i}(y)=\inf\{\sum_{i=1}^k\sigma_{U_i}(y_i):\sum_{i=1}^k y_i=y\}\). Thus an intersection counterpart generally introduces a decomposition of the support direction, rather than summing supports at the same direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under relative-interior qualification, an intersection’s support function is the infimal convolution of the component support functions.
assumptions_latex: \(U_i\subseteq\mathbb R^m\text{ is nonempty, closed, and convex.}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_{\cap_iU_i}(y)=\inf_{\sum_i y_i=y}\sum_{i=1}^k\sigma_{U_i}(y_i).\)
review_flags: The exact qualification and attainment conditions need a convex-analysis source.

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Function Composition Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical support-function identities for scaling, linear images, Minkowski sums, products, and qualified intersections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the support function of a nonempty set \(U\) by \(\sigma_U(y)=\sup_{u\in U}y^\top u\). For compatible linear maps \(A\), one has \(\sigma_{AU}(y)=\sigma_U(A^\top y)\). For \(\alpha>0\), \(\sigma_{\alpha U}(y)=\alpha\sigma_U(y)\), while \(\sigma_{0U}(y)=0\). For nonempty sets \(U,V\), \(\sigma_{U+V}(y)=\sigma_U(y)+\sigma_V(y)\), with equality in the extended-real sense, and Cartesian products separate blockwise. If \(U,V\) are closed and convex and satisfy \(\operatorname{ri}U\cap\operatorname{ri}V\ne\varnothing\), then \(\sigma_{U\cap V}(y)=\inf_{y_1+y_2=y}\{\sigma_U(y_1)+\sigma_V(y_2)\}\). These identities determine whether canonicalization uses substitution, addition, or auxiliary direction-splitting variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear images use adjoint substitution; positive scaling multiplies the support value, zero scaling gives zero; Minkowski sums and products separate additively; and qualified intersections use infimal convolution.
assumptions_latex: \(U,V\text{ are nonempty subsets of compatible finite-dimensional spaces.}\)
\(U,V\text{ are closed and convex with }\operatorname{ri}U\cap\operatorname{ri}V\ne\varnothing\text{ for the intersection identity.}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_{AU}=\sigma_U\circ A^\top,\quad \sigma_{\alpha U}=\alpha\sigma_U\text{ for }\alpha>0,\quad \sigma_{0U}=0,\quad \sigma_{U+V}=\sigma_U+\sigma_V,\quad \sigma_{U\cap V}=\sigma_U\mathbin{\square}\sigma_V.\)

notation.meaning: infimal convolution of f and g
adjoint matrix of A in Euclidean coordinates

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Linear-Inequality Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SOC reformulation of rowwise affine inequalities with Euclidean-ball coefficient uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each row \(i\), let the uncertain coefficient be \(a_i(u_i)=\bar a_i+P_i u_i\), where \(\|u_i\|_2\le1\), and let \(b_i\) be fixed. Then \(a_i(u_i)^\top x\le b_i\) for every admissible \(u_i\) is equivalent to \(\bar a_i^	op x+\|P_i^	op x\|_2\le b_i\). Therefore a system of independently uncertain linear inequalities has an exact SOCP counterpart consisting of one SOC inequality per row.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each linear inequality with ellipsoidal coefficient uncertainty becomes one second-order-cone inequality involving its nominal value and uncertainty radius.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\bar a_i+P_i u_i)^\top x\le b_i\ \forall\|u_i\|_2\le1\iff \bar a_i^	op x+\|P_i^	op x\|_2\le b_i.\)

notation.meaning: nominal coefficient vector in row i
